news.headline: Pope to be discharged days after lung cancer surgery
news.story_lead: Pope Leo XIV, seen here on his way to hospital, is to be discharged less than a week after he announced his diagnosis - Published 25 minutes ago Pope Leo XIV will be discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday afternoon, just four days after an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung. The Vatican said the Pope will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing to a crowd in St Peter's Square on Sunday, as he did last week when he surprised the world by announcing the surgery. On Friday, photographs were released of the Pope celebrating Mass and distributing communion in hospital for staff.
news.full_article_text: Pope Leo XIV, seen here on his way to hospital, is to be discharged less than a week after he announced his diagnosis - Published 25 minutes ago Pope Leo XIV will be discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday afternoon, just four days after an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung. The Vatican said the Pope will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing to a crowd in St Peter's Square on Sunday, as he did last week when he surprised the world by announcing the surgery. On Friday, photographs were released of the Pope celebrating Mass and distributing communion in hospital for staff. A statement from his doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray showed "steady improvement" following his operation. The surgery on Tuesday, which lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung. The results of further tests to check for any sign that the cancer has spread have not yet been announced. The Pope also spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, in their first call since June 2025. The Vatican said the call was to urge "dialogue and peace". It came as Russia's bombardment of cities across Ukraine intensifies, with a growing number of civilian casualties and no sign of Putin being ready to halt the invasion. The Pope also called for a humanitarian ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshkiy, occupied by Russia and under constant shelling, to allow people to be evacuated and for the urgent delivery of food and medicine. The BBC recently reported on residents there being forced to eat garden weeds to survive. The Pope's schedule has been cleared completely until 20 October, so his reappearance in public so soon is a surprise and will be some relief for Catholics around the world. Those close to the Pope said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America, planned for early November and which includes a visit to Peru, where he was a missionary for many years. It is not yet clear whether he might be fit to travel or require further treatment. news.headline: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD
news.story_lead: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force arrested a government doctor and two others after busting an alleged mephedrone manufacturing unit in Balotra. A government doctor was among three people arrested after Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted an alleged mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit at a house in Balotra district on Saturday. Police seized 3.764 kg of raw MD, chemicals and equipment, ₹ 3.41 lakh in cash and a car.
news.full_article_text: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force arrested a government doctor and two others after busting an alleged mephedrone manufacturing unit in Balotra. A government doctor was among three people arrested after Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted an alleged mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit at a house in Balotra district on Saturday. Police seized 3.764 kg of raw MD, chemicals and equipment, ₹ 3.41 lakh in cash and a car. The ANTF team, with assistance from local police, raided the premises in the Siwana police station area after receiving information about an alleged MD manufacturing unit, deputy inspector general of police Abhijeet Singh said. Police identified the three arrested men as prime suspect Suresh Kumar Vishnoi (27), a resident of Mithora; Dr Mukesh Vishnoi (29), and Utkarsh Vishnoi (19), a resident of Modran village in Jalore district. From failed government job aspirant to alleged MD manufacturer Suresh completed his graduation and attempted several government recruitment examinations, including those for patwari, gram sevak, Rajasthan Police, forest guard and police sub-inspector posts, but failed to secure a government job, an ANTF officer said. In 2022, he moved to Bengaluru with a friend and began working in pharmaceutical sales as a medical representative. After working in the field for around two years, he allegedly found the earnings insufficient. Police said Suresh returned to his village in 2024 and came into contact with people involved in drug trafficking. He allegedly began purchasing, selling and supplying MD before deciding to manufacture it himself in pursuit of higher profits. Investigators suspect that he learnt the process of manufacturing MD by watching videos on YouTube and other social media platforms. He allegedly used chemicals and equipment to prepare the drug at his house in Mithora. According to the ANTF, Suresh had called Dr Mukesh Vishnoi and Utkarsh Vishnoi to his house to sell a consignment of MD. The two allegedly arrived in a car. Police suspect that Suresh used Dr Mukesh’s contacts to supply the drug in and around Jalore and Siwana. During questioning, Suresh allegedly disclosed details about supplying MD through his associates and other people involved in drug trafficking. Raw MD, chemicals and equipment seized The ANTF team had received information that Suresh was operating an MD manufacturing unit at his house and in the adjoining premises. After verifying the information, the team conducted a raid with local police. Officers said that the three men were found sitting in a shed outside the house. A search of the house and surrounding premises led to the recovery of raw MD, chemicals and equipment allegedly used to manufacture and dry the drug. All three were arrested, and the seized material was taken into custody. The seized material included 3.764 kg of raw MD, including its packaging, and two packets of powder allegedly used in manufacturing the drug, weighing 888 grams including the plastic bags. Police also seized 800 grams of methylene dichloride (MDC) and 514 grams of a chemical described in the seizure details as isopropyl acid. The equipment recovered from the premises included an electric churning machine, an induction cooktop, a large glass jar, a thermometer and a piece of cloth bearing a substance allegedly used in drying MD. In addition, the team seized ₹ 3,41,700 in cash and a Kia Seltos bearing registration number RJ-19-CT-10351.

news.full_article_text: HT Evening Brief October 17: Abhijeet Dipke gets conditional bail; Supreme Court backs children’s internet rights Here's a quick recap of the day's top headlines from India, the world and the field of sports and entertainment. Good evening! Here's your 5-minute wrap of the day's top headlines from across the country and the world. Abhijeet Dipke granted conditional bail upon signing peace bond CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was granted conditional bail on Saturday, a day after he was detained on his way to Connaught Place and subsequently arrested. Dipke has been released by the special executive magistrate subject to a conditional bail bond. One of the primary conditions would be to ensure there is no breach of peace on his end for a period of one year. Read more here . ‘Children have fundamental right to internet access’: Supreme Court The right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual, including children irrespective of their age, the Supreme Court has held, cautioning that blanket restrictions on children’s internet access in the name of safety risk undermining their freedom, privacy and ability to seek help when they encounter online abuse. Read more here . US Congressman claims H-1B holders from India, China replacing Americans US Congressman Riley Moore has alleged that H-1 B visa holders are replacing American computer science graduates, claiming employers are turning to foreign workers willing to accept lower wages. In a post on X accompanying a snippet of his television interview, Moore called the H-1B and Optional Practical Training (OPT) programmes “SCAMS” and alleged that they undercut and replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. Read more here . Yashasvi Jaiswal's non-selection for New Zealand ODIs unfair: R Ashwin Former India off-spinner R Ashwin was displeased when Yashasvi Jaiswal was omitted from the squad for the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand, beginning November 4. The BCCI announced the squads for the ODI and Test assignments on Friday evening, and Jaiswal didn't make the cut despite Shubman Gill not being a part of the team for the final two ODIs. Read more here . Legendary music composer Deva dies at 75 Legendary music composer Deva died on October 17 at the age of 75. The man who composed the famous intro music that Rajinikanth now uses in all his films suffered a heart attack and was admitted to a private hospital before his death. Khushbu Sundar expressed shock at the news, having met the composer just 10 days before his death. news.exam_corner_topic: Supreme Court orders autism patients on stem cell therapy to register on Centre’s portal
news.headline: Supreme Court orders autism patients on stem cell therapy to register on Centre’s portal
news.story_lead: Supreme Court orders autism patients on stem cell therapy to register on Centre’s portal The Centre must launch a portal for autism patients undergoing stem cell therapy and issue a protocol explaining rules for clinical trials and research, the SC said. The Supreme Court has directed the Centre to create a dedicated online portal for patients undergoing stem cell therapy for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) within six weeks. The court also made it mandatory for such patients, their parents, guardians, caregivers and also the treating medical practitioners and clinics administering such therapy to maintain an extensive database.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court orders autism patients on stem cell therapy to register on Centre’s portal The Centre must launch a portal for autism patients undergoing stem cell therapy and issue a protocol explaining rules for clinical trials and research, the SC said. The Supreme Court has directed the Centre to create a dedicated online portal for patients undergoing stem cell therapy for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) within six weeks. The court also made it mandatory for such patients, their parents, guardians, caregivers and also the treating medical practitioners and clinics administering such therapy to maintain an extensive database. The order, passed on October 13 and uploaded on Friday, comes in the backdrop of the court’s January 30 order prohibiting the use of stem cell therapy as a routine clinical service, directing it only to be undertaken only within an approved and monitored clinical trial or research setting. A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and R Mahadevan said, “As regards patients who had already commenced stem cell therapy for ASD on or before January 30, 2026, we direct the Union to establish a dedicated online portal…Such online portal is to be created within a period of 6 weeks from the date of this order.” The particulars to be given on the portal included the medical records of such patients, including the particulars of the treating medical practitioners, the nature and course of the intervention administered, and such other clinical details as specified on the portal. The bench directed the Centre to ensure appropriate safeguards for the confidentiality and security of the patients’ medical information. Last month, the court had directed the Centre to disclose how many applications for clinical trials were received pursuant to its January 30 order. It further asked the Centre to indicate steps being taken to shift those ASD patients already undergoing stem cell therapy as of January 30 into a regulated research framework. The Centre filed an affidavit on September 28 which said that pursuant to January 30 no application for a clinical trial had been received. Regarding the other issue, the Centre stated that a multicenter randomised controlled trial (RCT) has been proposed to be set up at two tertiary care sites – one in north India and another in south India, within a period of six months. This will be funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). After reviewing the response, the court found that the proposed RCT does not lay down any eligibility criteria for patients already undergoing stem cell therapy for ASD. Further, there was no uniform platform for such patients or their caregivers to provide their information. After registering on the portal, the court said that until the RCT is established, patients who commenced stem cell therapy for ASD on or before January 30 will be permitted to continue therapy, as a “strictly temporary arrangement”. “This arrangement shall be confined to existing patients and shall not be construed as recognition or approval of stem cell therapy for ASD as a permissible clinical service,” the court added. The court further noted that the lack of easily accessible information about the use of stem cell therapy for ASD is a prime reason for many patients and their families to pursue such treatment. It granted the Centre six weeks to issue a comprehensive protocol clearly explaining the regulatory regime governing the use of stem cells in research and clinical trials relating to ASD. “The objective is to ensure that no stakeholder is left to navigate a labyrinth of regulatory instruments without being able to ascertain the precise requirements applicable to them,” the order said. The court directed the Centre to clearly inform the public that stem cell therapy for ASD is not permissible as a clinical service outside a duly approved and monitored research or clinical trial setting. Such information was ordered to be put out in a dedicated and easily identifiable section of the Ministry of Health’s official website in a clear and accessible language. “The need of the hour is to clearly explain the existing regulatory framework applicable to research/clinical trial corresponding to different levels of manipulation of stem cells for ASD,” the bench said. It was critical of the Centre and various authorities concerned in this field for failing to curb this malpractice due to a lack of readily accessible information to the public. “The failure of the authorities to effectively curb the malpractice of illegally administering a prohibited form of medical intervention as a clinical service has led to the proliferation of clinics and doctors offering such services. The lack of readily accessible information, which the public could consult to ascertain the legal position, has tacitly enabled such malpractice to continue,” the court said. The bench allowed the Parents’ Forum for Stem Cells in Autism and Cerebral Palsy to make their suggestions to the Centre while formulating the proposed design of the RCT. It also asked the Centre what mechanism will be available for those patients excluded from receiving the intervention under RCT as they too are continuing the treatment as per the present arrangement. The order required the Centre to deliberate upon this issue and place a comprehensive plan for the continued monitoring and medical supervision of such participants, including appropriate follow-up, assessment of their clinical condition and such further measures as may be necessary to safeguard their health and well-being. The court further clarified its January 30 order to suggest that the prohibition is on the use of stem cell being administered as a “therapy” for ASD based on the availability of scientific evidence and the prevailing regulatory framework in the country. However, “It does not amount to an immutable prohibition against any future development in this field,” it added. The court sought compliance report from the Centre before the next date of hearing on December 14.

news.headline: Sapphire International School Students Visit ISRO to Study India's Space Missions
news.story_lead: Students from Sapphire International School undertook an educational visit to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to learn about India's space missions. The exposure visit was aimed at inspiring young minds and fostering an interest in space science and technology.
news.full_article_text:
### Educational Visit to ISRO

Students from Sapphire International School participated in an experiential visit to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). The tour provided the students with direct exposure to India's space endeavors and technological capabilities.

* **Core Focus:** Exploring India's major space missions, satellite applications, and space exploration programs.
* **Objective:** Fostering scientific temper and encouraging students to pursue careers in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) fields.
bullet_points: Students of Sapphire International School visited ISRO facilities.
The tour offered insights into India's space achievements and research initiatives.
The initiative aims to promote scientific awareness and STEM education among school children.
key_facts: Sapphire International School organized an educational tour to ISRO.
The primary topic of exploration was India's ongoing and past space missions.
exam_relevance: Relevant for understanding scientific outreach and awareness programs by national research organizations.
Connects with educational policy efforts to promote STEM education and scientific temper among students.
news.upsc_analysis: Educational visits to primary scientific bodies such as ISRO serve as vital practical learning opportunities, inspiring young students toward scientific research and fulfilling the constitutionally recognized duty to cultivate inquiry and scientific thinking.
causes: The drive to enhance practical learning and promote interest in space science among school students.
impacts: Increased awareness among school children about national space capabilities and technology careers.
government_steps: Support for student engagement and public outreach activities by national science institutions like ISRO.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Article 51A(h) of the Indian Constitution, which emphasizes the duty to develop a scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry.
way_forward: Sustain and broaden youth outreach programs across educational institutions to build early capacity in technology and scientific research.

news.headline: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
news.story_lead: - Published 4 hours ago Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue. Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. news.full_article_text: - Published 4 hours ago Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue. Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro. Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon. Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%. The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil. Why the Amazon rainforest is so important What in the World podcast Jair Bolsonaro promoted mining in indigenous lands in the Amazon and forest clearances soared at the same time as resources to protect the forest were cut. During Bolsonaro's presidency from 2019 to 2022, the Amazon lost nearly 60% more in forest lands compared to the previous four years, news agency AFP reported, citing official data. Lula reversed his policies and oversaw deforestation rates drop to a six-year low during his first year in office. Lula tightened up environmental monitoring and penalties for illegal logging. "Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he said in a post on X on Friday. Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species. In a healthy state, they absorb vast quantities of planet-warming carbon dioxide, helping to keep the Earth cool. But they have come under increasing pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create conditions for wildfires. Brazil's Environment Minister Joao Paulo Capobianco described the decline in Amazon deforestation as "absolutely stratospheric". It was an "historic achievement" for Brazil, said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima. It showed that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions", Astrini said. news.headline: Mumbai shipping manager among 3 sanctioned by EU for Russia trade
news.story_lead: Mumbai shipping manager among 3 sanctioned by EU for Russia trade Vigor Marine Services LLP was sanctioned because its two vessels were allegedly involved in transporting crude oil or petroleum products from Russia. A Mumbai-based commercial ship manager was among three individuals and nine entities sanctioned by the European Union for being involved in the import of sanctioned goods to Russia and circumventing EU sanctions related to oil and financial transactions. Vigor Marine Services LLP was sanctioned because its two vessels were allegedly involved in transporting crude oil or petroleum products originating in Russia and “practicing irregular and high-risk shipping practices”, the European Council said in a statement.
news.full_article_text: Mumbai shipping manager among 3 sanctioned by EU for Russia trade Vigor Marine Services LLP was sanctioned because its two vessels were allegedly involved in transporting crude oil or petroleum products from Russia. A Mumbai-based commercial ship manager was among three individuals and nine entities sanctioned by the European Union for being involved in the import of sanctioned goods to Russia and circumventing EU sanctions related to oil and financial transactions. Vigor Marine Services LLP was sanctioned because its two vessels were allegedly involved in transporting crude oil or petroleum products originating in Russia and “practicing irregular and high-risk shipping practices”, the European Council said in a statement. The high-risk activities included having “inadequate liability insurance, engaging in ship-to-ship transfers and manipulating the vessels’ Automatic Identification System”, the statement said. Also Read I 'We're done': Ukraine's Zelensky says won't follow Trump's demand of no strike on Russian refineries The latest sanctions also targeted Hurus Trade FZE, a Dubai-based trading intermediary in the crude oil sector “supplying Russian-origin crude oil to India, in particular to Nayara Energy Limited, an entity listed under [EU] restrictive measures”. Abetment of Russia’s war The EU has sanctioned a limited number of India-based individuals and entities on charges of either allegedly supporting Russia’s military and industrial complex or helping in the export of Russian energy. In October last year, three New Delhi-based firms providing a range of services for the aviation industry were among 45 entities sanctioned by the EU. The new measures, unveiled on Thursday, were put in place as part of further action against individuals and companies circumventing EU sanctions to aid and abet “Russia’s illegal war of aggression”, EU foreign and security policy chief Kaja Kallas said. Noting that EU sanctions have denied Russia of more than €1 trillion, she said: “We will continue to make it harder and more expensive for Russia to continue its war.” Others targeted by the latest sanctions include Movers Group LLC, a Russia-based cargo delivery company involved in the parallel import of goods subject to EU restrictive measures, and its general director Dmitry Chudovsky, and LLC DT Inier and its majority shareholder Ivanna Savchuk. LLC DT Inier was described as a licensed Russian customs broker and logistics operator involved in “decentralised sanctions circumvention schemes”, a charge also levelled against Begler Tekstil Insaat Elektronik ve Dis Ticaret Ltd and Medse Group LLC, both trade companies based in Türkiye and operating a global network. The EU also sanctioned United Stream LLC and its founder, Svetlana Gumenyuk. United Stream is a financial services company registered in Russia that “acts as a payment agent and intermediary, likewise facilitating the import of EU goods subject to restrictive measures”. Also Read I Trump waives some Russia-related sanctions that threatened 100% tariffs on India As part of measures targeting the circumvention of oil-related EU sanctions, sanctions were imposed on Vigor Marine Services, United Arab Emirates -based DIS Logistics DMCC, and Seychelles-based Shiva Shipping Ltd, which were described as being “part of the shadow fleet ecosystem”. Those listed under the EU sanctions regime are subject to an asset freeze, and the provision of funds or economic resources, directly or indirectly, to them or for their benefit is prohibited. Additionally, a travel ban to the EU applies to the persons listed. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. Read More

A Mumbai-based commercial ship manager was among three individuals and nine entities sanctioned by the European Union for being involved in the import of sanctioned goods to Russia and circumventing EU sanctions related to oil and financial transactions.

Vigor Marine Services LLP was sanctioned because its two vessels were allegedly involved in transporting crude oil or petroleum products originating in Russia and “practicing irregular and high-risk shipping practices”, the European Council said in a statement.
The high-risk activities included having “inadequate liability insurance, engaging in ship-to-ship transfers and manipulating the vessels’ Automatic Identification System”, the statement said.

news.headline: India-Canada trade sees double-digit growth amid PM Modi's December visit
news.story_lead: India-Canada trade sees double-digit growth amid PM Modi's December visit Data comes as the two countries had what experts described as one of the “biggest weeks” in bilateral relations. Even as the two countries await the conclusion of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), merchandise trade between Canada and India has already increased by double digits between January and August this year. Citing data from Statistics Canada, the Asia-Pacific Foundation of Canada pointed out that goods trade is “already humming along”, with Canada’s merchandise exports to India from January to August 2026 amounting to CA$ 3.03 billion, up 36.7 per cent year-over-year.
news.full_article_text: India-Canada trade sees double-digit growth amid PM Modi's December visit Data comes as the two countries had what experts described as one of the “biggest weeks” in bilateral relations. Even as the two countries await the conclusion of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), merchandise trade between Canada and India has already increased by double digits between January and August this year. Citing data from Statistics Canada, the Asia-Pacific Foundation of Canada pointed out that goods trade is “already humming along”, with Canada’s merchandise exports to India from January to August 2026 amounting to CA$ 3.03 billion, up 36.7 per cent year-over-year. “That jump is the sixth-largest among Canada's 27 "principal trading partners" as defined by Statistics Canada,” it noted. Canadian metals and minerals exports to India topped the list, comprising 41 per cent of those exports, followed by agri-food at 16.9 per cent. Canada’s merchandise imports from India over the same period totalled CA$ 7.05 billion, up 10.2 per cent year-over-year. In 2025, Canadian merchandise exports to India totalled CA$3.9 billion, and imports amounted to CA$9.7 billion. That data comes as the two countries had what Vina Nadjibulla, co-founder and CEO of the Centre for Strategic Statecraft, described as one of the “biggest weeks” in bilateral relations. “We’re seeing something remarkable,” Nadjibulla said, adding, “There’s a lot of momentum, quite a bit of political will.” She said that beyond CEPA, other conversations will progress in parallel, including on mobility. The movement in India-Canada relations The two Prime Ministers, Narendra Modi and Mark Carney, had a telephone conversation on Tuesday, even as Canadian minister of foreign affairs Anita Anand travelled to the country and minister of international trade Maninder Sidhu led a nearly 300-strong trade mission. After completing the Team Canada Trade Mission, Sidhu said it had secured 34 commercial agreements valued at close to CA$300 million for Canadian businesses. “From energy and critical minerals to aerospace, Canadian companies have built valuable connections that will strengthen our long-term partnership with one of the world's fastest-growing major economies. Canada is ready to be the reliable partner India needs, and the opportunities secured on this mission will deliver lasting benefits for our workers and businesses,” he added in a release issued by Global Affairs Canada, the country’s foreign ministry, on Friday. Sidhu also met commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal to “advance negotiations” towards the CEPA. Five negotiating rounds have been completed, and negotiators are expected to meet twice as they aim to conclude talks by December, the deadline set by the two PMs. Sidhu and Goyal have met 10 times since May 2025, the release stated. With Modi’s bilateral visit to Canada scheduled for the second week of December, the trajectory of the renewed relationship could remain positive. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Anirudh Bhattacharyya Anirudh Bhattacharya is a Toronto-based commentator on North American issues, and an author. He has also worked as a journalist in New Delhi and New York spanning print, television and digital media. He tweets as @anirudhb. Read More

news.headline: Heavy security deployment continues across central Delhi a day after ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest
news.story_lead: Heavy security deployment continues across central Delhi a day after ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest Delhi Police has stepped up security at Jantar Mantar, Connaught Place and key offices amid the possibility of fresh protests, a day after 2,000 joined the CJP rally. Heavy security deployment continued across central Delhi on Saturday, with barricades at Jantar Mantar and additional personnel outside the Delhi Police and Election Commission of India headquarters amid the possibility of fresh protests by left-wing organisations, a day after nearly 2,000 people gathered in and around Connaught Place for the “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest. No major protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) or the Congress party have been announced so far in the city.
news.full_article_text: Heavy security deployment continues across central Delhi a day after ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest Delhi Police has stepped up security at Jantar Mantar, Connaught Place and key offices amid the possibility of fresh protests, a day after 2,000 joined the CJP rally. Heavy security deployment continued across central Delhi on Saturday, with barricades at Jantar Mantar and additional personnel outside the Delhi Police and Election Commission of India headquarters amid the possibility of fresh protests by left-wing organisations, a day after nearly 2,000 people gathered in and around Connaught Place for the “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest. No major protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) or the Congress party have been announced so far in the city. Barricades remain in place at Jantar Mantar, which has been de-notified as a designated protest site, and security personnel are manning all three entry and exit points, near the Ashoka Road roundabout and along Tolstoy Marg and Sansad Marg. Additional barricades have been put up on Ashoka Road and Jai Singh Road to prevent crowding, as gatherings are prohibited across the New Delhi area under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), an officer aware of the matter said. Deep Dive Security has also been stepped up outside the Delhi Police headquarters and the Election Commission of India headquarters following information that some left-wing organisations may hold a women’s march outside the police headquarters, alleging sexual violence by police during the protests. “Through our intelligence branch officials, we have learnt that some left groups have planned a march outside the police headquarters later in the morning. Since no permission has been given to anyone to hold protests in the New Delhi area, no gathering will be allowed anywhere in central Delhi. Our security arrangements are in place to handle any flash protest,” the officer added. A senior police officer said that more than 200 companies of central armed paramilitary forces (CAPFs), comprising nearly 20,000 men and women, are available with the Delhi Police to handle protests across Delhi. The largest deployments of the CAPFs have been made in central Delhi, particularly in and around Jantar Mantar, Sansad Marg, the Election Commission headquarters and Connaught Place, as well as outside the residences of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and other key ministers. Nearly 10,000 Delhi Police personnel have also been kept in reserve to deal with demonstrations and marches in the city, the officers said. On Friday evening, nearly 2,000 people gathered in and around Connaught Place for the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest, scheduled to be held at Central Park at 5 pm. As police permission was not granted for the protest, Delhi Police and CAPF personnel were deployed in large numbers in Connaught Place and its adjoining areas from Thursday. By Friday noon, hundreds of personnel had taken over Central Park and closed all its access gates to ensure nobody entered the park. Outside the park, nearly 200 personnel, particularly from the CAPFs, formed a human chain around it as protesters in small groups began marching around Connaught Place’s inner circle after 5 pm. Senior police officers also conducted flag marches along the pavements and restricted movement near the site, including that of journalists. By 7.30 pm, police dispersed protesters from the Connaught Place area. Nearly 150 people were detained from the area, Mandi House and Janpath by 9 pm and were later released. “Police deployment is still in place in Connaught Place to avoid any protest and maintain law and order as markets are open today,” another police officer said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karn Pratap Singh Karn Pratap Singh has been writing on crime, policing, and issues of safety in Delhi for almost a decade. He covers high-intensity spot news, including terror strikes, serial blasts and security threats in the national capital. Read More - Election Commission Of India

news.story_lead: A magistrate court in Delhi has issued a fresh bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in connection with a 2018 criminal defamation case. The judicial order was issued after court officials reported that his residence was locked when they attempted to deliver an earlier summons notice.
news.full_article_text:
Judicial Magistrate First Class (South East) Rahul Jain issued a fresh bailable warrant against content creator Dhruv Rathee regarding a criminal defamation lawsuit filed against him in 2018. The complaint was lodged by Vikas Sanskrityayan over a video published on Rathee's YouTube channel titled 'BJP IT Cell Part II', which the complainant alleges contained false and defamatory claims targeting him.

The magistrate directed the issuance of the bailable warrant after being informed that process servers were unable to serve a summons notice at Rathee's residence because the property was locked. The court has scheduled the matter for its next proceedings on October 31, while a detailed formal order remains awaited.

Earlier in the week, the court had advanced the hearing date, which was originally set for November 20, following an urgent application by the complainant seeking preponement. The application highlighted that Rathee, who usually resides abroad in Austria or Germany, was currently present in India. Consequently, fresh summons were issued on October 12 to be served at his Gurugram address in Haryana. Records indicate that Rathee was initially summoned by the judicial court in this matter back in 2019.
news.background_context: The defamation complaint originates from a 2018 video posted on YouTube titled 'BJP IT Cell Part II'. The complainant, Vikas Sanskrityayan, alleges that the content circulated false statements that harmed his reputation. The judicial court first issued summons to Dhruv Rathee in relation to this case in 2019.

Courts issue bailable warrants as a formal process step when summons cannot be successfully served due to unavailable or locked premises, ensuring the presence of named individuals in legal proceedings.

hindi_translation.headline: 2018 के मानहानि मामले में दिल्ली अदालत ने यूट्यूबर ध्रुव राठी के खिलाफ नया जमानती वारंट जारी किया
hindi_translation.story_lead: दिल्ली की एक मजिस्ट्रेट अदालत ने 2018 के आपराधिक मानहानि मामले में यूट्यूबर ध्रुव राठी के खिलाफ नया जमानती वारंट जारी किया है। यह अदालती आदेश तब आया जब प्रक्रिया अधिकारियों ने बताया कि पहले का समन तामील कराने के प्रयास के दौरान उनका घर बंद पाया गया था।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
न्यायिक मजिस्ट्रेट प्रथम श्रेणी (दक्षिण पूर्व) राहुल जैन ने ध्रुव राठी के खिलाफ 2018 में दायर एक आपराधिक मानहानि मामले में नया जमानती वारंट जारी किया। यह शिकायत विकास सांस्कृत्यायन द्वारा राठी के यूट्यूब चैनल पर पोस्ट किए गए 'बीजेपी आईटी सेल पार्ट II' नामक वीडियो को लेकर दर्ज कराई गई थी, जिसमें शिकायतकर्ता ने आरोप लगाया था कि इसमें उनके खिलाफ झूठे और मानहानिकारक दावे किए गए थे।

मजिस्ट्रेट ने जमानती वारंट जारी करने का निर्देश तब दिया जब अदालत को सूचित किया गया कि राठी के आवास पर समन तामील नहीं कराया जा सका क्योंकि संपत्ति बंद पाई गई थी। अदालत ने अगली कार्यवाही के लिए 31 अक्टूबर की तारीख तय की है, जबकि विस्तृत आदेश का इंतजार है।

इससे पहले, अदालत ने शिकायतकर्ता के एक आवेदन पर सुनवाई की तारीख को 20 नवंबर से पहले कर दिया था। आवेदन में कहा गया था कि ऑस्ट्रिया या जर्मनी में रहने वाले राठी वर्तमान में भारत में मौजूद हैं। इसके बाद 12 अक्टूबर को नया समन जारी किया गया था जिसे उनके गुरुग्राम स्थित पते पर तामील कराया जाना था। रिकॉर्ड के अनुसार, राठी को पहली बार 2019 में इस मामले में समन भेजा गया था।
hindi_translation.background_context: मानहानि की यह शिकायत 2018 में 'बीजेपी आईटी सेल पार्ट II' शीर्षक से अपलोड किए गए एक यूट्यूब वीडियो से संबंधित है। शिकायतकर्ता का आरोप है कि वीडियो में झूठे बयान दिए गए थे। अदालत ने पहली बार 2019 में राठी को समन जारी किया था।
bullet_points: दिल्ली की अदालत ने 2018 के मानहानि मामले में ध्रुव राठी के खिलाफ नया जमानती वारंट जारी किया।
समन तामील कराने के दौरान गुरुग्राम स्थित घर बंद मिलने के बाद वारंट जारी किया गया।
यह मामला 'बीजेपी आईटी सेल पार्ट II' नामक यूट्यूब वीडियो को लेकर विकास सांस्कृत्यायन द्वारा दर्ज कराया गया था।
न्यायिक मजिस्ट्रेट राहुल जैन ने अगली सुनवाई 31 अक्टूबर तय की है।
राठी के भारत में होने की जानकारी मिलने पर अदालत ने सुनवाई की तारीख पहले खिसका दी थी।
समन 12 अक्टूबर को उनके गुरुग्राम (हरियाणा) पते पर तामील कराने के निर्देश दिए गए थे।
अदालत ने सबसे पहले 2019 में ध्रुव राठी को इस मामले में समन भेजा था।

news.headline: US Control Over Satellite Tech and Starshield's Role in Ukraine-Russia Conflict
news.story_lead: SpaceX's Starshield network, built upon Starlink satellite technology, plays a strategic role in the ongoing Ukraine-Russia conflict. The dependence on US-controlled satellite infrastructure highlights the growing impact of private space technology on modern military battlefields.
news.full_article_text:
### Overview of Starshield and Satellite Tech in Warfare

Starshield is SpaceX's specialized satellite network designed for government and defense applications, leveraging commercial Starlink architecture. In modern warfare, high-speed, low-latency satellite communication is critical for operational coordination, command, and intelligence sharing.

### Strategic Implications

- **Technology Foundation:** Derived from SpaceX's Starlink satellite architecture to serve military and government end-users.
- **Geopolitical Dynamics:** The reliance of military operations on US-controlled commercial satellite systems highlights how control over space technology can influence battlefield capabilities.
- **Modern Defense Evolution:** Represents the transition toward utilizing commercial low-Earth orbit (LEO) constellations for military communication and reconnaissance.
bullet_points: Starshield is a satellite-based network developed by SpaceX tailored for government and defense applications.
The technology is derived from SpaceX's commercial Starlink satellite constellation.
Satellite technology has become a central component of battlefield operations in the Ukraine-Russia conflict.
US control over critical space technology shapes operational capabilities in strategic defense scenarios.
The involvement of commercial satellite providers underlines the shifting dynamics of modern military communications.
key_facts: Starshield is developed by SpaceX using Starlink satellite technology.
The network serves military and defense functions during the Ukraine-Russia war.
Control over the technology resides under US jurisdiction and private corporate operations.

exam_relevance: Relevant for UPSC Science & Technology topics related to space assets, low-Earth orbit satellites, and dual-use technologies.
Applicable to Defence & Security discussions on space security, commercial technology integration, and battlefield communication.
news.upsc_analysis: The deployment of SpaceX's Starshield underscores the rising strategic value of dual-use satellite constellations in contemporary warfare, highlighting both operational advantages and national security reliance on private space technology.

impacts: Enhanced communication and operational capabilities in conflict areas.

hindi_translation.headline: उपग्रह प्रौद्योगिकी पर अमेरिकी नियंत्रण और यूक्रेन-रूस संघर्ष में स्टारशील्ड की भूमिका
hindi_translation.story_lead: स्टारलिंक उपग्रह प्रौद्योगिकी पर आधारित स्पेसएक्स का स्टारशील्ड नेटवर्क यूक्रेन-रूस संघर्ष में एक महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभा रहा है। अमेरिकी नियंत्रण वाली उपग्रह प्रणाली पर निर्भरता आधुनिक युद्ध क्षेत्रों में निजी अंतरिक्ष प्रौद्योगिकी के बढ़ते प्रभाव को रेखांकित करती है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### उपग्रह प्रौद्योगिकी और युद्ध में स्टारशील्ड का अवलोकन

स्टारशील्ड स्पेसएक्स का एक विशेष उपग्रह नेटवर्क है जिसे सरकारी और सैन्य अनुप्रयोगों के लिए स्टारलिंक की वाणिज्यिक वास्तुकला का उपयोग करके विकसित किया गया है। आधुनिक युद्ध प्रणाली में, रीयल-टाइम संचार और नियंत्रण के लिए उच्च गति वाली उपग्रह कनेक्टिविटी आवश्यक है।

### रणनीतिक प्रभाव

- **तकनीकी आधार:** सैन्य और सरकारी उपयोग के लिए स्पेसएक्स के स्टारलिंक उपग्रह नेटवर्क पर आधारित।
- **भू-राजनीतिक गतिशीलता:** अमेरिकी निजी उपग्रह प्रणालियों पर निर्भरता दर्शाती है कि अंतरिक्ष प्रौद्योगिकी का नियंत्रण युद्धक्षेत्र की क्षमताओं को कैसे प्रभावित कर सकता है।
- **रक्षा क्षेत्र का विकास:** यह आधुनिक रक्षा रणनीतियों में निचली पृथ्वी की कक्षा (LEO) के उपग्रहों के बढ़ते उपयोग का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।
bullet_points: स्टारशील्ड स्पेसएक्स द्वारा विकसित एक उपग्रह नेटवर्क है जो सरकारी और रक्षा आवश्यकताओं के लिए बनाया गया है।
यह नेटवर्क स्पेसएक्स के वाणिज्यिक स्टारलिंक उपग्रहों पर आधारित है।
यूक्रेन-रूस युद्ध में उपग्रह संचार एक प्रमुख घटक बनकर उभरा है।
महत्वपूर्ण अंतरिक्ष प्रौद्योगिकी पर अमेरिकी नियंत्रण युद्धक्षेत्र की रणनीतिक क्षमताओं को प्रभावित करता है।
निजी उपग्रह प्रदाताओं की भागीदारी आधुनिक सैन्य संचार के बदलते पैटर्न को दर्शाती है।
key_facts: स्टारशील्ड का विकास स्पेसएक्स द्वारा स्टारलिंक तकनीक के आधार पर किया गया है।
यह प्रणाली सैन्य और रक्षा उपयोग के लिए बनाई गई है।
प्रौद्योगिकी का नियंत्रण और संचालन अमेरिकी क्षेत्राधिकार के तहत आता है।

Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution guarantees Indian citizens the fundamental right to assemble peaceably and without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions.
news.headline: Prakash Raj Vows Continuation of Anti-CEC Agitation Against Electoral Roll Revision
news.story_lead: Actor-activist Prakash Raj announced that peaceful nationwide protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls will persist despite police interventions. Speaking at a demonstration in Thiruvananthapuram, he asserted that citizens possess the constitutional right to question state authorities.
news.full_article_text:
### Anti-CEC Demonstrations and Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
Actor and civic activist Prakash Raj stated that nationwide peaceful demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls will continue uninterrupted. Speaking to journalists following a protest event at Manaveeyam Veedhi in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, he highlighted democratic freedoms and the legacy of national figures like Mahatma Gandhi, B.R. Ambedkar, and Bhagat Singh.

### Local Police Intervention and Public Statements
During the event in Thiruvananthapuram, local police briefly intervened prior to the start of the gathering, citing the lack of official permission to operate a microphone. Following a brief dialogue, authorities permitted the meeting to proceed. Raj questioned the requirement of administrative permissions for holding peaceful public demonstrations and criticized illegal detentions of demonstrators.

### Broader Mobilization and Related Developments
Raj noted that student groups, labor unions, and farmers' organizations intend to join the ongoing agitation against the electoral roll revision. He predicted that the movement could expand significantly beyond recent demonstrations at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The broader agitation has coincided with heightened security in central Delhi following the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' movement, detentions of activists, and statements of concern from United Nations human rights officials regarding mass detentions.
news.background_context: The public agitation stems from objections to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls supervised by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, leading to protests and detentions in locations including Delhi and Thiruvananthapuram.
bullet_points: Actor-activist Prakash Raj addressed a protest gathering at Manaveeyam Veedhi in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
The protest targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Raj asserted that constitutional rights allow citizens to conduct peaceful public demonstrations.
Farmers, trade unions, and student bodies are expected to participate in upcoming phases of the nationwide movement.
The ongoing agitation has seen heavy police deployment in central Delhi following the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest.
Recent detentions included CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke, while AISA leader Neha Bora was released.
The United Nations expressed concern over mass detentions connected to the anti-Election Commission demonstrations in Delhi.

Mains (GS Paper II): Electoral reforms, administrative accountability, role of civil society in a constitutional democracy, and balance between law and order and freedom of assembly.
news.upsc_analysis: The news highlights the civic friction surrounding electoral processes and public demonstration rights. In Indian governance, the Election Commission of India is mandated to maintain credible voter rolls via revisions such as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Concurrently, public agitations underscore the interplay between fundamental rights under Article 19(1)(b) and administrative regulations governing public assemblies and permissions.

hindi_translation.headline: प्रकाश राज ने कहा: मतदाता सूची पुनरीक्षण के खिलाफ सीईसी विरोधी आंदोलन जारी रहेगा
hindi_translation.story_lead: अभिनेता-कार्यकर्ता प्रकाश राज ने घोषणा की है कि मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार और मतदाता सूची के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) के खिलाफ देशव्यापी शांतिपूर्ण विरोध प्रदर्शन जारी रहेंगे। तिरुवनंतपुरम में एक सभा को संबोधित करते हुए उन्होंने कहा कि नागरिकों को अधिकारियों से सवाल करने का संवैधानिक अधिकार है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त विरोधी प्रदर्शन और विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR)
अभिनेता और सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता प्रकाश राज ने कहा कि मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार और मतदाता सूची के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) के खिलाफ देशव्यापी शांतिपूर्ण विरोध प्रदर्शन जारी रहेंगे। तिरुवनंतपुरम, केरल के मानवीयम वीधी में आयोजित एक विरोध सभा के बाद पत्रकारों से बात करते हुए, उन्होंने लोकतांत्रिक स्वतंत्रता और महात्मा गांधी, बी.आर. आंबेडकर और भगत सिंह की विरासत को रेखांकित किया।

### स्थानीय पुलिस का हस्तक्षेप और बयान
तिरुवनंतपुरम में कार्यक्रम की शुरुआत से पहले स्थानीय पुलिस ने लाउडस्पीकर/माइक का उपयोग करने की अनुमति न होने का हवाला देते हुए हस्तक्षेप किया। संक्षिप्त बातचीत के बाद पुलिस ने सभा को जारी रखने की अनुमति दी। प्रकाश राज ने शांतिपूर्ण प्रदर्शनों के लिए अनुमति की आवश्यकता पर सवाल उठाया और प्रदर्शनकारियों को हिरासत में लिए जाने की आलोचना की।

### व्यापक लामबंदी और संबंधित घटनाक्रम
प्रकाश राज ने कहा कि छात्र संगठन, श्रमिक संघ और किसान संगठन मतदाता सूची पुनरीक्षण के खिलाफ चल रहे इस आंदोलन में शामिल होंगे। उन्होंने अनुमान जताया कि यह आंदोलन दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर पर हुए प्रदर्शनों से भी बड़ा रूप ले सकता है। यह घटनाक्रम दिल्ली में 'लहरा दो तिरंगा' प्रदर्शन के बाद सुरक्षा बढ़ाए जाने, कार्यकर्ताओं की हिरासत और संयुक्त राष्ट्र मानवाधिकार अधिकारियों द्वारा जताई गई चिंताओं के बीच सामने आया है।
hindi_translation.background_context: यह विरोध प्रदर्शन मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार की देखरेख में चलाए जा रहे मतदाता सूची के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) से उपजे असंतोष से संबंधित है।

माइक की अनुमति न होने के कारण पुलिस ने शुरू में हस्तक्षेप किया, लेकिन बाद में कार्यक्रम की अनुमति दी।
राज ने कहा कि संवैधानिक अधिकार नागरिकों को शांतिपूर्ण विरोध करने की अनुमति देते हैं।
किसान, मजदूर संघ और छात्र संगठन आंदोलन के अगले चरणों में भाग लेंगे।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने दिल्ली में हुई हिरासतों पर चिंता व्यक्त की है।

news.exam_corner_topic: Fundamental Right to Internet Access for Children & Social Media Restrictions
static_gk: Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution guarantees freedom of speech and expression to all citizens.
Article 21 guarantees protection of life and personal liberty, which the judiciary has interpreted to encompass various fundamental rights.

In Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020), the Supreme Court ruled that freedom of speech and expression and the right to carry on trade/business via the internet are constitutionally protected under Article 19.
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act was enacted in 2012 to protect children from sexual abuse, harassment, and pornography.
news.headline: Supreme Court Rules Internet Access a Fundamental Right for Children, Rejects Blanket Social Media Bans
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India declared that access to and use of the internet is a fundamental right for every individual, including children regardless of their age, under Articles 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution. The bench observed that blanket prohibitions on children accessing digital platforms are disproportionate and counterproductive to child safety.
news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Ruling on Children's Right to Digital Access

In an order dated October 15, 2026, a Supreme Court bench comprising Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Chandran ruled that internet access is a fundamental right flowing from Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) read with Article 19(1)(a) (Freedom of Speech and Expression) of the Constitution. The court asserted that children, irrespective of their age, possess these rights equally and cannot be subjected to blanket digital bans.

### Context of the Decision

The judgment emerged while the apex court was examining measures for detecting and removing Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) from internet platforms. Addressing the global debate on restricting social media for minors through complete age bans, the bench stated that protecting children should not mean depriving them of essential digital tools necessary for education, information, and social connection. For children in remote areas or those with special needs, the internet often serves as a vital tool for learning and community support.

### Risks of Total Prohibitions

The bench highlighted that blanket prohibitions fail to prevent internet usage and instead drive children toward unregulated and riskier digital spaces. Furthermore, such bans could instill fear among children who face online harassment, grooming, or extortion, preventing them from reporting incidents to parents or authorities due to fear of disciplinary action for accessing the web. This would directly frustrate the primary objective of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.

### Responsibility of Platforms and Regulatory Safeguards

The court emphasized that the burden of online safety must fall on digital platforms and perpetrators of harmful material rather than restricting the victims. Rather than total bans, the court suggested structural digital safeguards, including:
- Parental consent mechanisms for pre-teens.
- Default private accounts for minors.
- Dedicated 'child modes' restricting adult contacts and unvetted advertising.
- Age-appropriate digital safety and sex education covering consent, privacy, and abuse reporting.

The bench clarified that its ruling does not prevent the government from restricting access to inherently harmful content, such as adult-content websites.

### Parallel Petition on Social Media Age Limits

Separately, a Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notices to the Union Government, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Ministry of Law and Justice, and the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR). This was in response to a petition filed by Emerald Heights International School (Indore) seeking a legal framework to enforce age restrictions and regulate social media use by minors.
news.background_context: In the landmark 2020 ruling Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, the Supreme Court established that exercising freedom of speech and conducting trade through the internet are protected under Article 19 of the Constitution. However, the question of whether basic internet access itself constituted an independent fundamental right was left open until this decision extended constitutional guarantees to minors.

### SC Judgment on Digital Rights for Children
- **Core Ruling:** Internet access is a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) for all citizens, including children.
- **Key Principles Introduced:**
  1. **Principle of Proportionality:** Blanket bans on digital access or social media for minors are disproportionate and counterproductive.
  2. **Victim-Centric Protection:** Responsibility for safety lies with platforms and authorities, not by restricting children.
  3. **Interconnection of Rights:** Digital access is critical for education, social inclusion (especially for special needs/remote children), and speech.
- **Policy Recommendations:**
  - Implement 'child mode' accounts by default.
  - Combine digital safety with age-appropriate education.
  - Ensure enforcement of the POCSO Act without scaring young victims into silence.

hindi_translation.headline: सुप्रीम कोर्ट का फैसला: बच्चों के लिए इंटरनेट पहुंच एक मौलिक अधिकार, सोशल मीडिया पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध अनुचित
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने फैसला सुनाया है कि इंटरनेट तक पहुंच और उसका उपयोग संविधान के अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) और 21 के तहत बच्चों सहित प्रत्येक व्यक्ति का मौलिक अधिकार है। पीठ ने कहा कि बच्चों की इंटरनेट पहुंच पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध लगाना अवांछनीय और सुरक्षा के दृष्टिकोण से उल्टा असर डालने वाला है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### बच्चों के डिजिटल अधिकारों पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट का निर्णय

15 अक्टूबर 2026 के एक आदेश में, जस्टिस जेबी पारदीवाला और जस्टिस केवी चंद्रन की सुप्रीम कोर्ट पीठ ने माना कि इंटरनेट तक पहुंच संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21 (जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार) और अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) (वाक एवं अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता) से जुड़ा एक मौलिक अधिकार है। अदालत ने स्पष्ट किया कि बच्चे, चाहे उनकी उम्र कुछ भी हो, इन अधिकारों के समान रूप से हकदार हैं।

### निर्णय की पृष्ठभूमि

यह निर्णय तब आया जब अदालत इंटरनेट से बाल यौन शोषण सामग्री (CSEAM) का पता लगाने और उसे हटाने के उपायों पर विचार कर रही थी। सोशल मीडिया पर न्यूनतम आयु सीमा या पूर्ण प्रतिबंध लगाने की बहस पर अदालत ने कहा कि बच्चों की सुरक्षा का मतलब उन्हें शिक्षा, सूचना और सामाजिक संपर्क के साधन से वंचित करना नहीं हो सकता। दूरदराज के क्षेत्रों के बच्चों और विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों के लिए इंटरनेट सीखने का एक महत्वपूर्ण जरिया है।

### पूर्ण प्रतिबंध के खतरे

पीठ ने चेतावनी दी कि पूर्ण प्रतिबंध बच्चों को असुरक्षित और अनियमित वेबसाइटों की ओर धकेल सकता है। इससे ऑनलाइन उत्पीड़न या शोषण का सामना करने वाले बच्चे सजा के डर से अपने अभिभावकों को जानकारी देने से डरेंगे, जिससे पोक्सो (POCSO) अधिनियम का मूल उद्देश्य विफल हो सकता है।

### डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्म की जवाबदेही

अदालत ने कहा कि सुरक्षा का बोझ बच्चों पर डालने के बजाय प्लेटफॉर्मों और हानिकारक सामग्री फैलाने वालों पर होना चाहिए। पूर्ण प्रतिबंध के बजाय अदालत ने डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से निजी खाते, चाइल्ड मोड और माता-पिता की सहमति जैसे उपायों का सुझाव दिया।

### अन्य याचिका पर सुनवाई

अलग से, भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्यकांत और न्यायमूर्ति जोयमाल्या बागची की पीठ ने इंदौर के एमरैल्ड हाइट्स इंटरनेशनल स्कूल की याचिका पर केंद्र सरकार और एनसीपीसीआर को नोटिस जारी किया है, जिसमें सोशल मीडिया के नियमन और आयु-आधारित प्रतिबंधों की मांग की गई है।
hindi_translation.background_context: 2020 के अनुराधा भसीन मामले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने माना था कि इंटरनेट के माध्यम से भाषण और व्यवसाय की स्वतंत्रता अनुच्छेद 19 के तहत संरक्षित है। नवीनतम निर्णय ने इस अधिकार को बच्चों के लिए भी स्पष्ट रूप से विस्तारित किया है।

निर्णय 15 अक्टूबर 2026 को जस्टिस जेबी पारदीवाला और जस्टिस केवी चंद्रन की पीठ द्वारा सुनाया गया।
यह टिप्पणी बाल यौन शोषण सामग्री (CSEAM) को हटाने से जुड़े मामले की सुनवाई के दौरान की गई।
अदालत ने सोशल मीडिया पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंधों को प्रभावहीन और उल्टा असर डालने वाला बताया।
पूर्ण प्रतिबंध बच्चों को असुरक्षित डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्मों पर जाने और POCSO के तहत रिपोर्टिंग से रोक सकते हैं।
प्लेटफॉर्मों के लिए 'चाइल्ड मोड', डिफ़ॉल्ट प्राइवेट अकाउंट और अभिभावक सहमति का सुझाव दिया गया।
डिजिटल सुरक्षा और आयु-उपयुक्त यौन शिक्षा को एक साथ लागू करने की आवश्यकता जताई गई।
सीजेआई सूर्यकांत की पीठ ने सोशल मीडिया विनियमन से जुड़ी एक अलग याचिका पर केंद्र को नोटिस दिया।

hindi_translation.story_lead: हेल्थकेयर क्षेत्र की प्रमुख निवेश फर्म ऑर्बीमेड ने दुनिया भर में जीवन विज्ञान (लाइफ साइंसेज) कंपनियों को वित्तीय सहायता देने के लिए $3 अरब जुटाए हैं। यह पूंजी बायोटेक्नोलॉजी, फार्मास्यूटिकल्स और स्वास्थ्य सेवा में नवाचार करने वाले उद्यमों को समर्थन प्रदान करेगी।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### जीवन विज्ञान क्षेत्र के लिए वैश्विक पूंजी जुटाव

स्वास्थ्य सेवा क्षेत्र में काम करने वाली निवेश फर्म ऑर्बीमेड ने वैश्विक जीवन विज्ञान क्षेत्र की कंपनियों में निवेश के लिए $3 अरब की पूंजी जुटाई है।

- **क्षेत्रीय प्रभाव:** इस निवेश का उद्देश्य दुनिया भर में क्लिनिकल अनुसंधान, नवाचार और बाजार विस्तार को गति देना है।
bullet_points: ऑर्बीमेड ने $3 अरब की कुल पूंजी प्रतिबद्धता हासिल की है।
यह राशि वैश्विक जीवन विज्ञान और स्वास्थ्य सेवा संस्थाओं के लिए निर्धारित है।
लक्षित क्षेत्रों में बायोटेक्नोलॉजी, फार्मास्यूटिकल्स और मेडिकल टेक्नोलॉजी शामिल हैं।
इसका उद्देश्य क्लिनिकल विकास और वैश्विक विस्तार को गति देना है।

news.headline: Pope pictured for first time since surgery and cancer diagnosis
news.story_lead: Pope Leo thanked medical staff as he was pictured for the first time since his lung surgery - Published 16 October 2026 Pope Leo XIV has been pictured celebrating Mass from hospital, in the first images of him released by the Vatican since he underwent lung surgery. The 71-year-old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications. The images shared on Friday showed the Chicago-born Pope wearing a green robe while standing behind a makeshift altar on the tenth floor of the hospital.
news.full_article_text: Pope Leo thanked medical staff as he was pictured for the first time since his lung surgery - Published 16 October 2026 Pope Leo XIV has been pictured celebrating Mass from hospital, in the first images of him released by the Vatican since he underwent lung surgery. The 71-year-old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications. The images shared on Friday showed the Chicago-born Pope wearing a green robe while standing behind a makeshift altar on the tenth floor of the hospital. Pope Leo "celebrated with the medical and nursing staff" and thanked workers for their service, the Vatican press office said. - Pope's cancer diagnosis leaves Catholics questioning what comes next Published 2 days ago Also on Friday, the Pope phoned Russian President Vladimir Putin from hospital to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where access to food and water has been cut off for thousands . "The fact that he accepted the call and spoke with the Pope may, I hope, be a sign that the Pope's request will indeed be carried out," said Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican's secretary of state. Without mentioning a ceasefire, the Kremlin said: "The Vatican's intention to help create the conditions necessary to ensure the safety of the town's population and to organise vital supplies has been supported". "It has been agreed to cooperate on this matter," it added. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Turk, made a similar plea to address what he described as a "desperate" situation in Oleshky. The Pope's doctors said on Friday tests had shown "a steady improvement in his general condition" since his surgery. His doctors said that a chest X-ray indicated "good recovery of the operated lung". The whole lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed "to ensure the procedure was radical", the Vatican said following the surgery. "After the operation, the Pope awoke normally and returned after a brief period of observation to his room," it said earlier, before he spent a "peaceful night" at the hospital. The pontiff is expected to remain at the hospital for about a week as he recovers Pope Leo first announced that he would be having the operation during his weekly Sunday prayers, telling the crowd in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a "well-contained" nodule on his lung "at an early stage" and advised him to have it removed. Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous, but after it was examined the medical team confirmed it was, "as suspected by pre-operative tests", the Vatican said. He was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma. The Vatican has stressed that the Pope had shown no symptoms of infection or illness prior to the procedure. news.headline: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
news.story_lead: Oregon school shooting: Police name victims and say suspect was former student - Published 17 October 2026, 00:02 BST An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and tried to wrestle away a shotgun from the arms of a teen suspect who opened fire on a special educational needs class. As she tussled with him on the floor of the class - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander ran inside. Armed with a .40-caliber pistol, he opened fire and killed the teen.
news.full_article_text: Oregon school shooting: Police name victims and say suspect was former student - Published 17 October 2026, 00:02 BST An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and tried to wrestle away a shotgun from the arms of a teen suspect who opened fire on a special educational needs class. As she tussled with him on the floor of the class - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander ran inside. Armed with a .40-caliber pistol, he opened fire and killed the teen. The bystander, a dad of two girls at the school, had been driving past Silver Rail Elementary in Bend when he saw the suspect firing in the car park then shooting through a window to enter. The details of the Thursday attack were confirmed by police, who said the 16-year-old suspect was a prior student at the school. Police say the suspect was armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class. "To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence, and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said on Friday. Police offered more information on the attack at at a news conference on Friday, where they identified two of the four victims. They include five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert. The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said. Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition. Krantz said the heroic actions of both the teacher and the father who ran inside the school saved lives. He said the teacher who wrestled with the gunman was not hurt but "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed". He identified the suspect as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, who previously attended the school and was a special educational needs student there. A search warrant has been executed at the suspect's home and a search is ongoing, the police chief said. Police believe the suspect travelled to the elementary school on foot, but police are still investigating his exact movements and how he acquired the gun. A motive is also not clear. Police identified two of the victims as five-year-old Rhoam Summer (left) and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert (right) Officials did not confirm the name of the father who intervened and fatally shot the suspect. But Kaylub Giamanco's family has identified him to US media as the person who sprang into action. The 36-year-old carpenter had just finished lunch and was on his way home when he passed the school, his brother told NBC News. He saw the suspect open fire on a vehicle outside the school then shoot through a window and go inside. Police said he had a legally concealed .40 caliber in his vehicle and his brother said he grabbed the pistol "and decided to go in after" the suspect. Police say he fired at the suspect "multiple times", killing him. In a statement to the BBC's partner CBS News, Giamanco's family said he is a "lifelong resident of Bend" and that he "is not seeking recognition". The family said Giamanco wants to express his "gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support". He and his family "respectfully ask for privacy". US President Donald Trump praised the bystander's actions on Friday, calling him a "great hero". Addressing reporters at the White House before departing for Georgia, Trump said the situation could have been "much worse" with no intervention. "It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it," he said. Without naming the bystander, Governor Kotek acknowledged the man's heroic actions stopping further loss of life, but noted they "carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well". Kayla Epstein contributed to this report. news.headline: Akal Takht declares AAP MLA Giaspura 'Tankhaiya' over alleged objectionable remarks
news.story_lead: Akal Takht declares AAP MLA Giaspura 'Tankhaiya' over alleged objectionable remarks Amritsar, The Akal Takht on Friday declared A MLA Manwinder Singh Giaspura 'Tankhaiya' over his alleged objectionable remarks against Sikh religious institutions and personalities. According to a statement issued by the Akal Takht secretariat, Giaspura, who represents Payal constituency in Ludhiana district, was denied entry into the secretariat on October 12 when a group of A MLAs and leaders visited the religious body over his alleged objectionable remarks against Sikh personalities and institutions in the past. Giaspura had allegedly told the media outside the secretariat, located in the Darbar Sahib complex, that he faced caste-based discrimination.
news.full_article_text: Akal Takht declares AAP MLA Giaspura 'Tankhaiya' over alleged objectionable remarks Amritsar, The Akal Takht on Friday declared A MLA Manwinder Singh Giaspura 'Tankhaiya' over his alleged objectionable remarks against Sikh religious institutions and personalities. According to a statement issued by the Akal Takht secretariat, Giaspura, who represents Payal constituency in Ludhiana district, was denied entry into the secretariat on October 12 when a group of A MLAs and leaders visited the religious body over his alleged objectionable remarks against Sikh personalities and institutions in the past. Giaspura had allegedly told the media outside the secretariat, located in the Darbar Sahib complex, that he faced caste-based discrimination. The statement said A legislators appeared at the secretariat on Friday in compliance with directions issued by the Jathedar Akal Takht Sahib. They admitted their mistake, acknowledging that despite the Jathedar's directions, they had neither contradicted Giaspura's allegations before the media on October 12 nor clarified that they had not faced any caste-based discrimination and that Giaspura had made inappropriate remarks, it said. The legislators present on Friday sought forgiveness from the 'Guru Sahib' and clarified that no one has ever been prevented from visiting Akal Takht Sahib based on caste, race or colour. The A MLAs and leaders also said they did not agree with Giaspura's remarks, calling them his personal views. Earlier, on Monday, a delegation of Punjab A MLAs submitted a memorandum to the Akal Takht Secretariat, seeking action against Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the alleged entry of Delhi Police into Gurdwara Bangla Sahib in the national capital during a protest. Calling it a grave violation of the sanctity of Sikh religious institutions, the MLAs urged the Akal Takht Jathedar to summon Shah and ensure accountability. Addressing the media, media adviser at the Akal Takht Secretariat, Jaskaran Singh, on Monday rejected Giaspura's statement alleging he was denied entry on the grounds of caste-based discrimination. He clarified that Giaspura was stopped because of his alleged past "derogatory, highly objectionable and threatening" remarks against the respected Jathedar Akal Takht and Sikh institutions. news.exam_corner_topic: Where is Dipke, asks CJP; lawyers meet Neha at RK Puram police station
news.headline: Where is Dipke, asks CJP; lawyers meet Neha at RK Puram police station
news.story_lead: Where is Dipke, asks CJP; lawyers meet Neha at RK Puram police station New Delhi, The Cockroach Janta Party on Friday said the whereabouts of its founder Abhijeet Dipke remained unknown after his detention by Delhi Police, while the All India Students' Association said its president Neha Bora had been traced to the RK Puram police station following hours of uncertainty over her location. AISA said Bora had been shifted from location to another across Delhi for five hours before its lawyers were able to meet her at RK Puram police station around midnight. It alleged that police had not clarified when she would be released and were refusing to provide her medicines despite knowing she has been unwell for the past few days.
news.full_article_text: Where is Dipke, asks CJP; lawyers meet Neha at RK Puram police station New Delhi, The Cockroach Janta Party on Friday said the whereabouts of its founder Abhijeet Dipke remained unknown after his detention by Delhi Police, while the All India Students' Association said its president Neha Bora had been traced to the RK Puram police station following hours of uncertainty over her location. AISA said Bora had been shifted from location to another across Delhi for five hours before its lawyers were able to meet her at RK Puram police station around midnight. It alleged that police had not clarified when she would be released and were refusing to provide her medicines despite knowing she has been unwell for the past few days. "Why is Delhi Police holding Neha until midnight in a police station? When will Neha be released? Why is a women student leader being put in a police station at midnight?" AISA said in a post on X. Deep Dive The CJP has alleged that Dipke had been taken to an undisclosed location and it had lost contact with him, while AISA had earlier said Bora was initially taken to an Anti-Narcotics Task Force, South-West District, facility before being shifted elsewhere. "The Delhi Police has taken Abhijeet Dipke to an undisclosed location. We have lost contact with him. He is not being allowed to talk to lawyers," the CJP said in a post on X. "Why does this government treat youth like terrorists? We are equal citizens of India and we deserve all the protections and rights of the Constitution!" it said. "Abhijeet was just walking out of his home with a Tiranga in his hand! How can walking with a tiranga be a crime?" the CJP asked, adding that detentions would not deter people from joining the protests. The CJP also wrote to Delhi Police inquiring about Dipke's whereabouts. In a letter addressed to Mandir Marg station house officer, CJP leader Rohan Deshpande said, "Since his detention, we have received no information regarding his present location or the police station or facility where he is being held.
