news.headline: Karnataka HC recalls order in land grab case linked to Kharge family, fresh hearing on Oct 30
news.story_lead: Karnataka HC recalls order in land grab case linked to Kharge family, fresh hearing on Oct 30 The Karnataka High Court recalled its earlier order in the Siddhartha Vihara Trust land case linked to the Kharge family and scheduled a fresh hearing for October 30. The Karnataka high court on Friday recalled its earlier order in a case involving the alleged illegal allotment of government land to the Siddhartha Vihara Trust, associated with the family of All India Congress Committee (AICC) president Mallikarjun Kharge, and scheduled a fresh hearing for October 30. A bench headed by Justice M.
news.full_article_text: Karnataka HC recalls order in land grab case linked to Kharge family, fresh hearing on Oct 30 The Karnataka High Court recalled its earlier order in the Siddhartha Vihara Trust land case linked to the Kharge family and scheduled a fresh hearing for October 30. The Karnataka high court on Friday recalled its earlier order in a case involving the alleged illegal allotment of government land to the Siddhartha Vihara Trust, associated with the family of All India Congress Committee (AICC) president Mallikarjun Kharge, and scheduled a fresh hearing for October 30. A bench headed by Justice M. Nagaprasanna passed the order after Mallikarjun Kharge’s son Rahul sought recall of the court’s August 18 order. The respondents will be heard before the court takes a fresh decision. The court’s latest order withdraws its directions to the 82nd City Civil and Sessions Court, reopening consideration of the proceedings concerning the alleged allotment of land by the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) and the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB) to the trust. On August 18, the Karnataka High Court had set aside proceedings initiated under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). It had also allowed the complainant to rectify defects in the affidavit and said the question of a police investigation could be considered subsequently. The case arises from allegations that the Siddhartha Vihara Trust received government land illegally. The complaint alleges that the BDA allotted about two acres of civic amenity land in the second block of BTM Layout Fourth Stage to the trust in 2014. About a decade later, another five acres near Bagalur were allegedly allotted to the trust through the KIADB, also citing educational purposes. The complainant has estimated the combined value of the two parcels at more than ₹ 240 crore. Mallikarjun Kharge, wife Radhabai Kharge, son Rahul Kharge, son-in-law Radhakrishna, Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge and INC leader M.B. Patil are among those named in the complaint. The land was subsequently reportedly returned. The complainant, however, alleged that no effective action was taken on a complaint submitted to the Lokayukta police. Lanchamukta Karnataka Vedike’s president Vijay Raghava Marathe later filed a private complaint seeking action in the matter. Marathe s advocate Lakshmi Aiyangar told HT that the withdrawal of the earlier order meant that the proceedings would now be reconsidered. “The High Court’s decision to recall its earlier order means the proceedings will be reconsidered. The next hearing on October 30 is expected to focus on the submissions of the parties and the further course of action in the case. The allegations remain subject to judicial consideration,” she said.

news.headline: Bihar: 1.4mn voters added in post-SIR roll in one year
news.story_lead: Bihar: 1.4mn voters added in post-SIR roll in one year The current electoral roll — last updated on October 1— has 75.5 million voters, roughly 1.4 million names more than the 74.1 million in September 2025 roll. Bihar’s electoral roll swelled by nearly 1.4 million names since the publication of the post-special intensive revision ( SIR ) in Bihar on September 30 last year, officials attached with the state electoral officer(CEO) have said. Bihar’s electoral roll swelled by nearly 1.4 million names since the publication of the post-special intensive revision ( SIR ) in Bihar on September 30 last year, officials attached with the state electoral officer(CEO) have said. The current electoral roll — last updated on October 1 this year — has 75.5 million voters, roughly 1.4 million names more than the 74.1 million in the September 2025 roll, published after the end of SIR. In this period, nearly 1.87 million people applied to be on the rolls using Form 6, the statutory application prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, for a person seeking inclusion of their name in an electoral roll. Out of these, 1.4 million applications have been successful, the officials quoted above said. “The number of enrolment goes up in an election year and then declines. It happens before the Lok Sabha , the legislative assembly or the panchayat polls,” said one of the officers quoted above on Wednesday. The additional 1.4 million names comprise people seeking to return to the rolls, new voters and young voters enrolling for the first time, said the second officer. The number of voters in Bihar went up by 4.19 million in 2023-24 — the year of Lok Sabha elections — and by 4.14 million in 2024-25, the year of assembly polls in the state. Prior to that, in 2022-23, the voter increase was 1.3 million, while in 2025-26, the increase was 2.45 million, said a second officer. All the 1.4 million people added to the post-SIR electoral roll, including new or first-time voters, have had to fill Form 6 for new enrolment. “Most people who enrolled after the SIR have applied online on the ECI portal,” said Kumud Kumari, a booth-level officer of Raja Bazar area in Patna. “At present, there is no electoral activity whatsoever. We as teachers are currently busy with academic activities in schools. Fresh enrolment to the voter list generally happens before elections through online applications.” The three-month SIR exercise in Bihar undertaken between June 25 and September 30, 2025 — the first in the country in the current series — initially removed 6.56 million people from the rolls, after 2.23 million voters were reported dead, 3.64 million shifted, and 0.68 million voters found to have their names at more than one location, out of the 78.9 million voters reported before the exercise. After the one-month scrutiny period between August 1 and September 1, 2025, during which aggrieved voters had to submit claims and objections, 2.15 million voters were added to the list and another 0.36 million removed, taking the number of electorate in the state to 74.1 million after the SIR. Bihar has not had a summary revision of the electoral roll since the 2025 SIR. In Kishanganj’s Thakurganj nagar panchayat, a booth-level officer received around 3,600 applications over the past year and recommended about 636 names for inclusion after verification. The BLO is also examining seven applications flagged as potential duplicates by the mobile application linked to the EC’s Demographic Similar Entry (DSE) software, which flags entries with similarities in names, fathers’ names and age. “I try my best to verify the documents of each voter before recommending the name to the ERO. The ERO then scrutinises it at his level before adding the voter,” said the BLO, requesting anonymity. In Patna, Siddheshwar Kumar Sharma, a government schoolteacher and BLO at booth No. 419 at the blind school in Kadamkuan, received about 24 applications over the past year. The development comes days after ECI told state election authorities that eligible citizens seeking enrolment need not submit a separate declaration – which seeks details of parental linkage to the previous SIR – along with Form 6. The Bihar CEO’s office has also been asked to conduct a campaign to identify and enrol first-time and left-out voters, according to a communication issued after a video conference of electoral officers on October 1. “Video conferences with EROs and district magistrates have been completed. Currently, training and orientation of officials is being done. We will begin the campaign this week itself,” said the second officer quoted above. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ruchir Kumar Ruchir writes on health, aviation, power and myriad other issues. news.headline: Madras HC allows RSS route marches on Oct 25, Nov 1; slams TN police over repeated rejections
news.story_lead: Madras HC allows RSS route marches on Oct 25, Nov 1; slams TN police over repeated rejections The Madras High Court permitted RSS route marches in Tamil Nadu on October 25 and November 1, criticising police for repeatedly rejecting applications on grounds already disapproved by the court. The Madras High Court on Friday permitted the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to hold its annual route marches across Tamil Nadu on October 25 and November 1, criticising the state police for repeatedly rejecting applications on grounds the court had already disapproved. Justice V Lakshminarayanan directed the police to coordinate with RSS organisers and finalise the timings and locations of the marches and subsequent public meetings by Monday.
news.full_article_text: Madras HC allows RSS route marches on Oct 25, Nov 1; slams TN police over repeated rejections The Madras High Court permitted RSS route marches in Tamil Nadu on October 25 and November 1, criticising police for repeatedly rejecting applications on grounds already disapproved by the court. The Madras High Court on Friday permitted the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to hold its annual route marches across Tamil Nadu on October 25 and November 1, criticising the state police for repeatedly rejecting applications on grounds the court had already disapproved. Justice V Lakshminarayanan directed the police to coordinate with RSS organisers and finalise the timings and locations of the marches and subsequent public meetings by Monday. “One thing must be said to the credit of the Tamil Nadu police. They have not come up with any novel reasons for rejection. They have consistently given the very reasons which this Court found as lame,” Justice Lakshminarayanan said. Deep Dive The Court was hearing a petition by RSS North Tamil Nadu secretary VG Jagadeesan. Jagadeesan**, through** senior advocate NL Rajah, had challenged police orders denying permission for the organisation’s annual route marches and public meetings as part of its Vijayadashami celebrations. The RSS had sought permission for processions on October 18, 25, and November 1 as alternative dates. The state police rejected the applications**,** citing places of worship belonging to other communities along the proposed routes, statues of rationalist leaders, traffic congestion, loudspeakers and possible law and order problems. The Court said that it had considered and disapproved these grounds in earlier proceedings. It said that the RSS had been moving the Court for permission for route marches since 2022. It referred to its previous decisions recognising the RSS’s right to conduct route marches, subject to lawful restrictions. The High Court also cited a 2023 order passed by one of its benches, which said that public roads remain secular spaces accessible to everyone irrespective of religion, caste or creed. “It is a classic case of using a scalpel, not for the purpose of an operation, but to kill the patient on whom the operation is sought to be performed,” the High Court said. During the hearing, Advocate General Vijay Narayan told the court that the state agreed to permit the marches on October 25 and November 1, subject to modifications suggested by local police authorities based on prevailing conditions. The RSS furnished details of the proposed routes, organisers, participant numbers and venues for public meetings. The court directed that these details form part of its order and recorded the organisation’s undertaking to comply with conditions imposed in earlier judicial proceedings. The Court said that police authorities must help applicants meet procedural requirements instead of looking for reasons to reject their requests. It also urged the RSS to submit applications sufficiently in advance and expressed hope that repeated disputes over route marches would no longer occupy the Court’s time. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ayesha Arvind Ayesha Arvind is a Senior Assistant Editor specialising in legal and judicial reportage. She covers High Courts and tribunals across southern India, and believes that important legal developments do not only come from New Delhi. Her work focuses on bringing significant decisions and developments from the region to a wider audience and explaining what they mean beyond the courtroom. She tries to make legal material accessible by translating legal jargon into clear, readable prose and putting pleas, lawsuits, judgments and legal developments in context. She also looks at their political realities and practical consequences for people. Ayesha is committed to the standards of integrity journalism requires. She places a premium on accuracy and fairness, and believes that journalism's powerful voice must be tempered by humility and a sense of proportion. Over almost two decades in journalism, she has covered law and order, civil law, crime and other areas of legal affairs. Her work includes breaking news, legal affairs stories, online analysis and commentary. Ayesha is deeply interested in the law, court judgments and the Constitution because they shape everyday life. news.headline: India rejects US lawmaker Pramila Jayapal’s remarks on voter roll revision as ‘interference in fellow democracy’
news.story_lead: India rejects US lawmaker Pramila Jayapal’s remarks on voter roll revision as ‘interference in fellow democracy’ India rejected US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s criticism of the voter roll revision, calling her remarks “unwarranted and uninformed”. India on Friday rejected senior US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal s criticism of the revision of the country’s electoral rolls as unwarranted and tantamount to interfering in the “electoral practices of a fellow democracy”. Jayapal, an Indian-origin lawmaker from the Democratic Party who has been a vocal critic of the Indian government, said on social media on Thursday that she was concerned about actions that appeared aimed at purging 130 million people from voting rolls.
news.full_article_text: India rejects US lawmaker Pramila Jayapal’s remarks on voter roll revision as ‘interference in fellow democracy’ India rejected US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s criticism of the voter roll revision, calling her remarks “unwarranted and uninformed”. India on Friday rejected senior US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal s criticism of the revision of the country’s electoral rolls as unwarranted and tantamount to interfering in the “electoral practices of a fellow democracy”. Jayapal, an Indian-origin lawmaker from the Democratic Party who has been a vocal critic of the Indian government, said on social media on Thursday that she was concerned about actions that appeared aimed at purging 130 million people from voting rolls. ALSO READ: India urges US to ensure safety of its citizens after alleged plot to target Hindu temple in Illinois When external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked about the matter at a regular media briefing, he replied: “We find the remarks of the Congresswoman unwarranted and uninformed and tantamount to interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy.” He added, “This is an approach that undermines democracy itself.” Jayapal, who was born in Chennai and moved to the US in 1982, said on social media that she was “deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls”. The move “appears to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing [in the US] to undermine voting rights in a democracy”, she said. “Protecting democracies everywhere is essential work, and the Indian people — like the American people — deserve free and fair elections. Non-violent resistance movements are essential in these moments and I stand with the Indian people who are engaging in non-violent protests to counter anti-democratic efforts in India,” she said. Jayapal’s comments came against the backdrop of protests in India by young people and opposition parties over alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has led to the striking off of millions of voters’ names. In December 2019, external affairs minister S Jaishankar had called off a meeting with US lawmakers after they reportedly declined to exclude Jayapal from the gathering. At the time, Jayapal had criticised restrictions imposed by the government in Jammu and Kashmir after the region’s special status was scrapped. “I have an interest in meeting people who are objective and open to discussion but not the people who already made up their minds,” Jaishankar had said at the time, after Jayapal introduced a resolution in the US House of Representatives that urged India to lift all restrictions on communications in Jammu and Kashmir. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. Read More

news.headline: Chaos at Chhattisgarh garba event as right-wing workers create ruckus over presence of Muslims
news.story_lead: Chaos at Chhattisgarh garba event as right-wing workers create ruckus over presence of Muslims A scuffle broke out on the stage during which Congress district president and former mayor Dheeraj Bakliwal was reportedly pushed. A garba event organised in Chhattisgarh's Durg descended into chaos on Wednesday after workers of right-wing groups reportedly created ruckus over the presence of Muslim youth at the event. A scuffle broke out on the stage during which Congress district president and former mayor Dheeraj Bakliwal was pushed, the Times of India reported.
news.full_article_text: Chaos at Chhattisgarh garba event as right-wing workers create ruckus over presence of Muslims A scuffle broke out on the stage during which Congress district president and former mayor Dheeraj Bakliwal was reportedly pushed. A garba event organised in Chhattisgarh's Durg descended into chaos on Wednesday after workers of right-wing groups reportedly created ruckus over the presence of Muslim youth at the event. A scuffle broke out on the stage during which Congress district president and former mayor Dheeraj Bakliwal was pushed, the Times of India reported. The videos of the incident were shared on social media that showed the right-wing workers on the stage raising objection over the presence of Muslim youth at the event. What led to the dispute According to reports, the dispute reportedly began after an NSUI office-bearer identified as Adil Khan shared a poster of the event on social media with details of the event and mentioning free entry passes. Deep Dive On Wednesday night when the garba event was underway, members of right wing outfits, Bajrang Dal and Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), reached the venue and barged on the stage. Heated exchange turned into a scuffle and Bakliwal was seen being pushed in one of the videos. The Congress leader was later quoted as saying that the entry to the event was free and anyone could attend it. However, VHP's Ramlochan Tiwari reportedly opposed to the participation of Muslims in the garba event and said entry checks should be made mor stringent. The police have registered a case on the complaint of the organisers and CCTV footage is being examined to identify the accused. Row over Gujarat garba event A garba event in Gujarat's Ahmedabad landed up in a row after non-Hindus and Muslims were asked to leave a high-end garba event in Ahmedabad amid ongoing Navratri festival. This prompted popular Gujarati folk singer Aditya Gadhvi to distance himself from the announcement, saying it was not his message, news agency PTI reported. Gadhvi was performing at the event. A video of the announcement has gone viral on social media, showing anchor-RJ Akash Trivedi on Wednesday asking non-Hindus and Muslims to leave the venue from the stage of the 'Rang Morla ft. Aditya Gadhvi' event organised at Savvana Party Plot on the city's Shela Road. "A humble request to any 'vidharmi' (non-Hindus) and Muslims to leave the ground. The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) has come here to protect Sanatan Dharma," Trivedi is heard saying in the video. "The VHP wants you (garba participants) to look around and report suspicious people to the helpline number," the RJ added. Gujarat VHP spokesperson Hitendrasinh Rajput defended the announcement, saying it was part of a routine exercise carried out by Bajrang Dal volunteers at garba (traditional folk dance from Gujarat) events in the state. "Usually, Bajrang Dal, the youth wing of the VHP, visits garba events in Ahmedabad and meets the organisers, asking them to prevent non-Hindus from entering the venue. Sometimes, they also apply tilak on the foreheads of men attending the events and remove suspicious people from the ground," Rajput was quoted as saying. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. In the meantime, she thought it was a good idea to share what she learnt, hence took up part-time teaching of journalism course at Jamia Millia Islamia, which she says, she thoroughly enjoyed-not sure if the feeling was mutual. For a year, she also tried her hands at communication roles, only to realise she was more comfortable with news. So, joined HT in September 2025. Not much of a talker, always up for chai and sarcasm. news.story_lead: Govt defends Jaishankar-Rubio meet in Mumbai amid Oppn criticism: 'Practice for last decade or so' As the Opposition questioned why the US envoy had announced Jaishankar's meetings, Rahul Gandhi said “Rubio has summoned his employee to Mumbai”. The government on Friday sought to address the opposition’s criticism of external affairs minister S Jaishankar travelling to Mumbai to meet US secretary of state Marco Rubio next week and said it has been a practice over the past decade for foreign dignitaries to be hosted outside New Delhi. Congress leaders had earlier criticised the government after US ambassador Sergio Gor said at a public event that “we expect…Jaishankar to be joining us [in Mumbai]” for Rubio's visit.
news.full_article_text: Govt defends Jaishankar-Rubio meet in Mumbai amid Oppn criticism: 'Practice for last decade or so' As the Opposition questioned why the US envoy had announced Jaishankar's meetings, Rahul Gandhi said “Rubio has summoned his employee to Mumbai”. The government on Friday sought to address the opposition’s criticism of external affairs minister S Jaishankar travelling to Mumbai to meet US secretary of state Marco Rubio next week and said it has been a practice over the past decade for foreign dignitaries to be hosted outside New Delhi. Congress leaders had earlier criticised the government after US ambassador Sergio Gor said at a public event that “we expect…Jaishankar to be joining us [in Mumbai]” for Rubio's visit. Rubio is set to travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar, and the capital is not part of his itinerary. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Jairam Ramesh had questioned why the US envoy had announced the external affairs minister’s meetings, with Gandhi saying “Rubio has summoned his employee to Mumbai”. Responding to questions on the opposition’s criticism that the external affairs minister had been “summoned” to Mumbai by the US, external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Jaishankar is set to host the United Arab Emirates (UAE)’s deputy prime minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Mumbai between October 19 and 20 before holding talks with Rubio. Noting that Jaishankar will also attend a celebration in Mumbai of the 250th anniversary of the independence of the US as the guest of honour, Jaiswal said: “It has been the practice for the last decade or so that we have hosted foreign dignitaries outside Delhi.” In this context, he said Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted his Spanish counterpart in Baroda, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Ahmedabad, and the Mauritius PM in Varanasi, while the external affairs minister hosted the foreign ministers of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Goa, the Botswana foreign minister at Kevadia in Gujarat, and the Heart of Asia conference in Amritsar. Jaiswal said UAE PM'visit is an opportunity to review all aspects of India-UAE cooperation under their comprehensive strategic partnership. “The two delegations will assess and take forward initiatives in the areas of energy, trade and investments, fintech, defence and connectivity,” he said. They will also have a detailed discussion on the situation in West Asia and global and multilateral issues. Rubio’s visit will allow both sides to review India-US ties and discuss ways to strengthen the bilateral comprehensive global strategic partnership. “Discussions are expected to cover key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade and investment, defence, critical and emerging technologies, and other areas of mutual interest,” Jaiswal said. The two sides will discuss regional and global developments, and the visit will be an opportunity to sustain high-level engagement between the two countries and advance shared priorities, he said. During his last visit to India in May, Rubio had participated in a Quad foreign ministers’ meeting and hosted a reception in New Delhi to mark the 250th anniversary of US independence. People familiar with the matter said Rubio will travel to Jamnagar for a few hours to visit facilities of energy major Reliance, which has partnered on the construction of America First Refining in Texas, the first new major oil refinery in the US in almost five decades. Reliance is also a major purchaser of energy from Venezuela, sales of which are controlled by the US administration. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. news.headline: Centre seeks Punjab govt report on activist Jhota’s murder, measures to prevent drug trafficking
news.story_lead: Centre seeks Punjab govt report on activist Jhota’s murder, measures to prevent drug trafficking The MHA has called for the implementation of key measures to support the national goal of a drug-free India. The Centre has sought a report from the Punjab government on the killing of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh, alias Jhota, and the steps taken to strengthen the state's anti-narcotics operations. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has asked the state government to submit a detailed account of the October 13 killing in Mansa, PTI reported.
news.full_article_text: Centre seeks Punjab govt report on activist Jhota’s murder, measures to prevent drug trafficking The MHA has called for the implementation of key measures to support the national goal of a drug-free India. The Centre has sought a report from the Punjab government on the killing of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh, alias Jhota, and the steps taken to strengthen the state's anti-narcotics operations. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has asked the state government to submit a detailed account of the October 13 killing in Mansa, PTI reported. It has also sought details of measures taken to combat drug trafficking and substance abuse. The MHA has called for the implementation of key measures to support the national goal of a drug-free India. These include setting up a dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), conducting financial investigations in drug-related cases and strengthening prosecution under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. Deep Dive The ministry has also stressed the need for better coordination through the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism. Other priorities include designating special NDPS courts, appointing nodal officers and taking action against transnational drug networks. How Parwinder Singh (Jhota) died Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight in Mansa on October 13 during a confrontation at a medical store over the alleged sale of addictive substances. He had been campaigning against drug abuse and the alleged illegal sale of habit-forming medicines at chemist shops. Jhota was known for confronting suspected sellers and recording videos of such encounters for social media, according to reports. On the day of the incident, he and his associates allegedly confronted a medical store owner over the sale of addictive drugs. The confrontation reportedly turned violent, with the shop owner allegedly opening fire. Jhota was killed, while others were injured. Protests, demand for CBI probe The killing triggered protests in Mansa and other parts of Punjab. Jhota's family refused to cremate his body and demanded action against those responsible. His supporters and several farmer organisations also called for a statewide bandh on October 16. Opposition parties and farmer groups backed demands for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe. Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Congress MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring criticised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the state's law-and-order situation and its handling of the drug menace. Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon demanded a CBI probe into Jhota's killing, while Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia called for the dissolution of the state government and the imposition of President's Rule. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.story_lead: 'Bhaag Neha Bhaag, Jantar Mantar Chalo': Delhi protests inspire online games where players take on roles of protesters, cops From gathering virtual crowds and dodging water cannons to escaping police chases, the Jantar Mantar protests have inspired a series of free online video games. Protests at Jantar Mantar are now inspiring online gaming experiences. news.full_article_text: 'Bhaag Neha Bhaag, Jantar Mantar Chalo': Delhi protests inspire online games where players take on roles of protesters, cops From gathering virtual crowds and dodging water cannons to escaping police chases, the Jantar Mantar protests have inspired a series of free online video games. Protests at Jantar Mantar are now inspiring online gaming experiences. Developers have created free online games inspired by the demonstrations, giving players virtual roles as protesters and police personnel in challenges involving crowds, barricades and detentions. From ‘ Jantar Mantar Chalo’, which lets players choose between protesters and police personnel, to ‘Bhaag Neha Bhaag’, inspired by AISA national president Neha Bora ’s attempts to reach the protest site, the games draw on recent political developments and the scenes that unfolded on the streets of the national capital. Another game, ‘Jantar Mantar to Jail’, features Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) members Abhijeet Dipke , Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Players must dodge falling jail bars and police personnel while collecting coins representing “accountability” and “democracy”. The games allows users to participate in virtual versions of events that have attracted attention online. ‘Bhaag Neha Bhaag’ takes inspiration from repeated detentions Inspired by the protests is ‘Bhaag Neha Bhaag’, created by 30-year-old screenwriter and filmmaker Anav Nayar. He co-founded Wizloop Studios with his brother, Akshay Nayar, with the company focusing on content strategy, intellectual property for brands and the creative use of AI, PTI reported. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Anav Nayar (@anavnayar) A post shared by Anav Nayar (@anavnayar) Nayar said the idea came from following Neha Bora’s attempts to reach Jantar Mantar and her repeated detentions. “We were following how Neha Bora and other protesters were trying to reach Jantar Mantar. They were detained but the very next day, they were back at the spot. “My brother Akshay asked me how they were managing to do it, and that got me thinking about creating a game around it,” Nayar told PTI. The brothers named the game Bhaag Neha Bhaag, drawing inspiration from the 1998 German film Run Lola Run, one of their favourites. ‘Jantar Mantar Chalo’ draws thousands of players Suraj Kushwah, a 27-year-old resident of Bareilly who works at a cloud gaming company, developed Jantar Mantar Chalo after watching news coverage of the protests. “I was watching the news and, out of sarcasm, thought of making a game around it,” Kushwah told PTI. A technology enthusiast, Kushwah used artificial intelligence (AI) tools and his gaming knowledge to develop the game in about one-and-a-half days. Players can choose to play as either protesters or Delhi Police personnel. Those playing as protesters must gather people and march towards Jantar Mantar, with larger crowds making them more powerful. Players choosing the police role, meanwhile, must detain as many protesters as possible. The game incorporates several elements associated with the demonstrations. Tear gas slows down protesters, while water cannons present another obstacle. Players can also dance in front of water cannons and interact with media personnel through interviews. Media coverage influences the game's progression. Interviews can increase a protester's influence and attract more people to the gathering. Its virtual map includes locations such as police stations, detention centres, India Gate and the Badarpur border. “I made it as a sarcastic take, but now that it is getting so much attention; I am looking at updating it further,” he said. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Naman Gangwar (@0xnaman) A post shared by Naman Gangwar (@0xnaman) ‘Jantar Mantar to Jail’ turns accountability into points The Nayar brothers also developed Jantar Mantar to Jail, which features CJP members Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Players choose one of the three characters and attempt to avoid obstacles, including falling jail bars and police personnel dressed in orange kurtas. Another game inspired by the protests features chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. It turns a satirical act involving a tap on his head into a scoring mechanic. Protest context to the games In June and July, the group led protests, including a march towards Parliament on July 20, demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister over repeated paper leaks and student suicides. He was forced to resign over a month later. The groups returned to the streets in October, joining opposition parties and student organisations in demonstrations seeking the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The protesters raised allegations concerning the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The demonstrations generated images, videos and online discussions that subsequently became a source of inspiration for the game developers. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Anita Goswami Anita Goswami is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, where she primarily covers Indian and international news. news.headline: Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora among 150 detained in Delhi; Oppn slams police action amid anti-CEC protests
news.story_lead: Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora among 150 detained in Delhi; Oppn slams police action amid anti-CEC protests At least 150 people were detained around Janpath Road, CP and Mandi House. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and AISA activist Neha Bora were among them. Delhi Police personnel at Abhijeet Dipke's door, his detention on the way to Connaught Place (CP) and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s claim that he was taken to an “undisclosed” location - the outfit's ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ call was marked by police action and a big crowd in central Delhi.
news.full_article_text: Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora among 150 detained in Delhi; Oppn slams police action amid anti-CEC protests At least 150 people were detained around Janpath Road, CP and Mandi House. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and AISA activist Neha Bora were among them. Delhi Police personnel at Abhijeet Dipke's door, his detention on the way to Connaught Place (CP) and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s claim that he was taken to an “undisclosed” location - the outfit's ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ call was marked by police action and a big crowd in central Delhi. At least 150 people were detained around Janpath Road, CP and Mandi House in Delhi. AISA activist Neha Bora was also among those picked up. As the day came to a close, both Dipke and Bora's teams claimed that they had no information on their whereabouts. Several Opposition leaders, including Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal and MK Stalin backed Dipke and Bora and called the situation in Delhi an “undeclared emergency”. The former Tamil Nadu chief minister also raised questions about their whereabouts after detention. CP not a notified protest site: Police to Dipke Earlier in the day, the CJP founder was served a notice by the Delhi Police and was asked not to join the rally. The notice cited prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS. The notice contended that Connaught Place was not a “notified protest site” as it asked Dipke not to hold the march. It also said that the CJP founder must refrain from infringing on the rights of other citizens. “Connaught Place is not a notified protest site and that demonstrations may be held at designated venues, subject to the necessary permission being sought and granted," a part of the notice read. The notice also pointed to CP being a hub for businesses and housing several prominent restaurants and outlets. “It (CP) houses a dense concentration of showrooms, restaurants, hotels, banks, offices and street vendors, so any disruption, particularly during evening and weekend hours, as well as the peak festival season, directly affects the livelihood of traders and their employees. Over 15 lakh traders and their employees depend on its peaceful and orderly functioning for the exercise of their fundamental right,” the notice read. The notice was personally handed to Abhijeet Dipke by the Delhi Police personnel at NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence. ‘I’m alone', Dipke tells cops moments before detention Abhijeet Dipke departed for the march site this evening and was detained by the police shortly after. However, a video from before his detention showed him asking the police how he was violating any laws. “Maine abhi violation kaise kiya hai? Main akela hoon (I am alone, how did I violate any order),” he said, asking how he had violated the law and pointing out that the others present were members of the media. CJP, AISA ask ‘where are Neha Bora, Abhijeet Dipke?’ Both the CJP and AISA sought to know Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora's whereabouts after they were detained on their way to the Tiranga rally. The outfits alleged that the two were being denied access to lawyers and associates after being detained by Delhi Police during protests in the national capital. "The Delhi Police has taken Abhijeet Dipke to an undisclosed location. We have lost contact with him. He is not being allowed to talk to lawyers," the CJP said in a post on X. "Why does this government treat youth like terrorists? We are equal citizens of India and we deserve all the protections and rights of the Constitution!" it said. In a post on X, AISA said Bora was being detained alone at the Anti-Narcotics Task Force in Mangolpuri. In a subsequent post, it claimed she is being taken from the Anti-Narcotics Task Force station, Mangolpuri, to an “undisclosed” location in a car with illegally blacked-out windows. Opposition rallies behind Dipke and Bora Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, and other Opposition leaders criticsed the Delhi Police action against Neha Bora and Abhijeet Dipke. "Abhijeet Dipke has been detained for holding the Indian National Flag. Let that sink in. In Independent India, our youth are being detained for peacefully asserting their democratic rights." Calling the action an “undeclared emergency”, she further said, “A government that fears dissent is now trying to intimidate an entire generation into silence. This is the conduct of a fascist regime that cannot tolerate a voice it cannot control.” Arvind Kejriwal said on X, “This is nothing but outright dictatorship. Is it a crime to hoist the tricolour? Abhijeet's arrest shows how much Modi ji fears them." Also Read: 'Hope better sense prevails': No urgent direction from SC against Dipke's CP 'Tiranga' march Former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin also sought to know where Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora are. “Detaining them without disclosing their whereabouts is blatantly illegal and deeply inhumane. The Union Government must release them immediately and stop suppressing peaceful protests. Every attempt to crush the movement will only make it stronger,” he wrote on X. Dipke, Bora and many others have been protesting against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and AISA activist Neha Bora were among them. Delhi Police personnel at Abhijeet Dipke's door, his detention on the way to Connaught Place (CP) and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s claim that he was taken to an “undisclosed” location - the outfit's ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ call was marked by police action and a big crowd in central Delhi.
hindi_translation.full_article_text: Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora among 150 detained in Delhi; Oppn slams police action amid anti-CEC protests At least 150 people were detained around Janpath Road, CP and Mandi House. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and AISA activist Neha Bora were among them. Delhi Police personnel at Abhijeet Dipke's door, his detention on the way to Connaught Place (CP) and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s claim that he was taken to an “undisclosed” location - the outfit's ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ call was marked by police action and a big crowd in central Delhi. At least 150 people were detained around Janpath Road, CP and Mandi House in Delhi. AISA activist Neha Bora was also among those picked up. As the day came to a close, both Dipke and Bora's teams claimed that they had no information on their whereabouts. Several Opposition leaders, including Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal and MK Stalin backed Dipke and Bora and called the situation in Delhi an “undeclared emergency”. The former Tamil Nadu chief minister also raised questions about their whereabouts after detention. CP not a notified protest site: Police to Dipke Earlier in the day, the CJP founder was served a notice by the Delhi Police and was asked not to join the rally. The notice cited prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS. The notice contended that Connaught Place was not a “notified protest site” as it asked Dipke not to hold the march. It also said that the CJP founder must refrain from infringing on the rights of other citizens. “Connaught Place is not a notified protest site and that demonstrations may be held at designated venues, subject to the necessary permission being sought and granted," a part of the notice read. The notice also pointed to CP being a hub for businesses and housing several prominent restaurants and outlets. “It (CP) houses a dense concentration of showrooms, restaurants, hotels, banks, offices and street vendors, so any disruption, particularly during evening and weekend hours, as well as the peak festival season, directly affects the livelihood of traders and their employees. Over 15 lakh traders and their employees depend on its peaceful and orderly functioning for the exercise of their fundamental right,” the notice read. The notice was personally handed to Abhijeet Dipke by the Delhi Police personnel at NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence. ‘I’m alone', Dipke tells cops moments before detention Abhijeet Dipke departed for the march site this evening and was detained by the police shortly after. However, a video from before his detention showed him asking the police how he was violating any laws. “Maine abhi violation kaise kiya hai? Main akela hoon (I am alone, how did I violate any order),” he said, asking how he had violated the law and pointing out that the others present were members of the media. CJP, AISA ask ‘where are Neha Bora, Abhijeet Dipke?’ Both the CJP and AISA sought to know Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora's whereabouts after they were detained on their way to the Tiranga rally. The outfits alleged that the two were being denied access to lawyers and associates after being detained by Delhi Police during protests in the national capital. "The Delhi Police has taken Abhijeet Dipke to an undisclosed location. We have lost contact with him. He is not being allowed to talk to lawyers," the CJP said in a post on X. "Why does this government treat youth like terrorists? We are equal citizens of India and we deserve all the protections and rights of the Constitution!" it said. In a post on X, AISA said Bora was being detained alone at the Anti-Narcotics Task Force in Mangolpuri. In a subsequent post, it claimed she is being taken from the Anti-Narcotics Task Force station, Mangolpuri, to an “undisclosed” location in a car with illegally blacked-out windows. Opposition rallies behind Dipke and Bora Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, and other Opposition leaders criticsed the Delhi Police action against Neha Bora and Abhijeet Dipke. "Abhijeet Dipke has been detained for holding the Indian National Flag. Let that sink in. In Independent India, our youth are being detained for peacefully asserting their democratic rights." Calling the action an “undeclared emergency”, she further said, “A government that fears dissent is now trying to intimidate an entire generation into silence. This is the conduct of a fascist regime that cannot tolerate a voice it cannot control.” Arvind Kejriwal said on X, “This is nothing but outright dictatorship. Is it a crime to hoist the tricolour? Abhijeet's arrest shows how much Modi ji fears them." Also Read: 'Hope better sense prevails': No urgent direction from SC against Dipke's CP 'Tiranga' march Former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin also sought to know where Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora are. “Detaining them without disclosing their whereabouts is blatantly illegal and deeply inhumane. The Union Government must release them immediately and stop suppressing peaceful protests. Every attempt to crush the movement will only make it stronger,” he wrote on X. Dipke, Bora and many others have been protesting against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: JDU MLA Anant Singh clarifies on ‘9 murders’ remark
news.story_lead: JDU MLA Anant Singh clarifies on ‘9 murders’ remark The JD(U) defended ex Bihar CM Nitish Kumar’s political record and rejected any suggestion of an association with criminal activity. Janata Dal (United) MLA Anant Kumar Singh on Friday claimed to have arranged the murder of nine people to help former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar during his political struggles. The ruling party was quick to distance itself from the controversial remark.
news.full_article_text: JDU MLA Anant Singh clarifies on ‘9 murders’ remark The JD(U) defended ex Bihar CM Nitish Kumar’s political record and rejected any suggestion of an association with criminal activity. Janata Dal (United) MLA Anant Kumar Singh on Friday claimed to have arranged the murder of nine people to help former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar during his political struggles. The ruling party was quick to distance itself from the controversial remark. Singh, who represents Mokama, made the claim while criticising the party’s decision to field his political rival, Neeraj Kumar, in the upcoming Bihar Legislative Council elections. He has vowed to ensure Neeraj Kumar’s defeat and is backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh. "Nitish Kumar and I go back a long way. To help him, I got nine people murdered. I stood by him in times when he was struggling to find a toehold," Singh said, as per PTI. ‘I was shot’ Singh later appeared to clarify. Speaking to ANI, he said nine of his associates were killed during Lalu Prasad Yadav ’s government and claimed that the killings were linked to their support for Nitish Kumar. He also said he had been shot during that period and that his family had suffered significant losses. “During the Lalu Yadav government, nine of my associates were killed, and I myself was shot. It was because we aligned ourselves with Nitish Kumar that Lalu Yadav had them killed. We have suffered such immense losses. My father also passed away due to a heart attack,” Singh told ANI. JD(U) responds The JD(U)'s national spokesperson Rajiv Ranjan Prasad said that the remark did not deserve serious consideration. In a video statement, Prasad, without naming Singh, defended Nitish Kumar’s political record and rejected any suggestion of an association with criminal activity. "Nitish Kumar has stood out for an untainted record, with no blemishes of hobnobbing with criminals and involvement in violence or any type of negativity," he said. "The type of statement that we have come across deserves no cognisance from the party and is unlikely to be taken seriously by the public," Prasad added. Political rivalry behind the remarks Singh’s outburst comes amid a dispute over the JD(U)’s choice of candidate for the upcoming Legislative Council polls. His opposition to Neeraj Kumar, a political rival, has put him at odds with the party leadership, even as he insists that his support for Anuj Singh does not reflect disloyalty to Nitish Kumar. Nitish Kumar, who has led Bihar for much of the past two decades, has built much of his political image around improving law and order in the state. His tenure has often been associated with the promise of ending the lawlessness that marked parts of Bihar’s earlier political landscape. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Anita Goswami Anita Goswami is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, where she primarily covers Indian and international news. With four years of industry experience, she has led coverage of Indian General elections, Assembly elections, and national polls in the United States, Canada, Bangladesh, and Nepal. As former Chief Copy Editor at Storytailors, she managed teams to produce top-quality content for networks like NDTV, Profit, CNBC-TV18, Upstox and News18. Her work is featured in NDTV, Meaww, and Global Pulse. Throughout her tenure, Anita has collaborated with and been mentored by top industry experts. news.headline: Bihar: Viral video shows three women, man consuming liquor inside Darbhanga hospital; police probe underway
news.story_lead: Bihar: Viral video shows three women, man consuming liquor inside Darbhanga hospital; police probe underway Darbhanga senior superintendent of police (SSP) Jagunath Raddi Jalaraddi directed the Benta police station in-charge to conduct a detailed investigation. A viral video purportedly showing three women and a man consuming liquor inside the surgical building of Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) has prompted a police inquiry, raising questions about security and discipline at the government-run healthcare institution. The video, which surfaced on Tuesday, purportedly shows the four near a staircase inside the hospital building.
news.full_article_text: Bihar: Viral video shows three women, man consuming liquor inside Darbhanga hospital; police probe underway Darbhanga senior superintendent of police (SSP) Jagunath Raddi Jalaraddi directed the Benta police station in-charge to conduct a detailed investigation. A viral video purportedly showing three women and a man consuming liquor inside the surgical building of Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) has prompted a police inquiry, raising questions about security and discipline at the government-run healthcare institution. The video, which surfaced on Tuesday, purportedly shows the four near a staircase inside the hospital building. The women have reportedly been described as sanitation workers, while the man has been identified as a trolley worker. However, their identities, employment status and the authenticity of the footage have not yet been officially established. The circulated footage purportedly shows women taking out snacks and disposable plastic glasses from a bag, followed by a man taking out a tetra pack of liquor from his waistband and handing it over. Hindustan Times has not independently verified the video or the circumstances in which it was recorded. Also read | Suspected phone snatcher left dangling from moving train in Bihar; video goes viral DMCH superintendent Dr Jagdish Chandra said the footage would be examined to verify its authenticity and establish the identities of the people and the location shown in it. He said he informed the police as soon as he learnt about the alleged incident. Chandra also said the Darbhanga district magistrate had asked him to ascertain the details and initiate appropriate action. The hospital's security in-charge, meanwhile, reportedly described the video as old. The footage is said to be around six months old, although its date of recording has not been officially confirmed. The inquiry is expected to establish when and where the alleged incident took place and whether the people seen in the video were actually hospital employees or outsourced staff on duty.

news.headline: Veteran BJP leader LK Advani admitted to Delhi's Apollo hospital with chest infection, condition stable
news.story_lead: Veteran BJP leader LK Advani admitted to Delhi's Apollo hospital with chest infection, condition stable LK Advani has been admitted to the pulmonary department and is under observation by a team of doctors. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) veteran leader Lal Krishna Advani was admitted to Apollo Hospital late Friday evening after complaining of a chest infection, officials said. He is currently undergoing treatment and his condition is stable.
news.full_article_text: Veteran BJP leader LK Advani admitted to Delhi's Apollo hospital with chest infection, condition stable LK Advani has been admitted to the pulmonary department and is under observation by a team of doctors. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) veteran leader Lal Krishna Advani was admitted to Apollo Hospital late Friday evening after complaining of a chest infection, officials said. He is currently undergoing treatment and his condition is stable. According to officials familiar with the matter, the 98-year-old was brought to the hospital at around 7:30 pm. He has been admitted to the pulmonary department and is under observation by a team of doctors. Hospital officials said the veteran leader is receiving treatment and remains stable. Advani, 98, was last admitted to Apollo Hospital in May this year due to age-related health issues. He remained in the hospital for a few days before being discharged. The BJP stalwart served as the party president during three terms: 1986-1990, 1993-1998 and 2004-2005. He served as Union home minister from 1998 to 2004 and deputy prime minister from 2002 to 2004 in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee . Advani's previous health issues In December 2024, the former deputy prime minister was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Indraprastha Apollo Hospital for medical management and investigations. He was under the care of neurologist Dr Vinit Suri, and the hospital said at the time that his condition was stable. On December 17, 2024, the hospital reported that Advani had shown gradual improvement and was likely to be shifted out of the ICU within the next one to two days, HT reported earlier. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ridhima Gupta Ridhima Gupta is a Principal Correspondent at Hindustan Times, where she covers healthcare, pharmaceuticals, and public health policy. Her reporting centers on Delhi’s major hospitals (AIIMS, Safdarjung, Lok Nayak), the state health department, and emerging medical trends. Ridhima is particularly interested in reporting on healthcare issues through the lens of women, children, and persons with disabilities. Her work often explores the intersection of healthcare and public policy, examining how these factors shape access health care. Based in New Delhi, many of her reports have led to direct government action over the years, in different city. Earlier this year, she completed a media training workshop on the Impact of Extreme Heat on Health, organised by the Global Strategic Communications Council (GSCC), further strengthening her interest in reporting on the intersection of climate change and public health. A postgraduate from the Asian College of Journalism, Chennai, Ridhima has around a decade of experience in journalism. She began her career as a trainee television reporter with Mirror Now in Mumbai and has since worked across multiple cities, including Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Delhi, contributing to both print and broadcast newsrooms. She is a recipient of the Laadli Media Fellowship (2022) for her reporting on education, disability, and women’s issues. Before joining Hindustan Times, Ridhima worked with The Times of India, New Indian Express and News18. A native of Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, Ridhima completed her undergraduate studies in Biotechnology. And when she is not working as a journalist she likes to paint and go on nature hikes. Read More

news.headline: Thousands march to Indian Supreme Court to demand election chief resign
news.story_lead: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend.
news.full_article_text: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi submitted a petition to the court challenging the process, in which tens of millions of names have been struck off the voter rolls. Opposition parties allege the revision benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. For weeks requests to protest had been denied by police, citing law and order reasons. Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained in Delhi. Gandhi called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march. In a press conference, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to Chief Justice Surya Kant, laying out their concerns with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged conduct. After they filed their petition later in the day, Kant responded by saying the matter was already before the court and therefore sub judice - meaning he could not speak about it. But he added: "You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law." There was a heavy security deployment in central Delhi and along the route of the march, with restrictions on traffic and on entry and exit at some metro stations. A bus carrying Gandhi and other opposition leaders made its way to the court from Barakamba road. Supporters waved flags and chanted his name as the Congress MP and others waved through the windows. Seated a few rows behind him was Neha Bora, a student leader who has gained prominence in the protests. A few kilometres on, in a place called Mandi House, the bus stopped and Rahul Gandhi and a few others climbed on top of the vehicle to wave at supporters lining up the street in the thousands. Many protesters climbed on to other buses parked here, while some waved flags and chanted anti-government slogans to the sound of drums and lots of cheering. "If they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?" one protester asked an AFP news agency reporter. Another protester called the march "a fight to save the very fabric" of India, the world's largest democracy. Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday Protesters have been demanding the country's the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud Over the past week, top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, have been briefly detained several times while leading protests in central Delhi. On Sunday, the CJP - which is not a registered political party - said it would continue protesting until Kumar stepped down. The CJP, which successfully led a protest over the summer that culminated in India's federal education minister's resignation, had called for a march on Saturday to Jantar Mantar - the best-known protest site in Delhi where the last set of sit-in demonstrations had also happened. But authorities in Delhi imposed overarching restrictions that made it almost impossible for protesters to travel and reach Jantar Mantar - trains were cancelled, dozens of metro stations were shut and tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were on the roads to detain protesters. The Home Ministry has now announced demonstrations will no longer be permitted at Jantar Mantar. Three other sites have been listed as alternatives should permission be granted. Monday's demonstrations come after thousands were detained over the weekend The CJP leaders - founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - were dramatically detained from a plane as they landed in Delhi to join the weekend protest. They were only released a day later - while Dipke returned home to attend his grandmother's funeral, Das and Ranka held a press conference where they said the protests would continue. Both leaders have said they will seek a new protest date from the police. Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses. The BBC also captured footage , external of a policeman slapping a detained protester inside a bus. The Delhi police did not respond to questions about the use of violence against protesters. In a statement, Reporters Without Borders condemned the detention of at least 16 Indian journalists. "Covering events of public interest is not a crime. It is their job. The police's actions against the press are unacceptable," it said. Rahul Gandhi said that young Indians who had come to peacefully protest with "love in their hearts, not hatred or anger" had been beaten up. BJP President Nitin Nabin accused opposition parties and the CJP of trying to destabilise India "at the behest of foreign forces" without elaborating on who the forces were. Related topics

news.exam_corner_topic: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
news.headline: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
news.story_lead: Verified video footage showed smoke above the presidential palace in Aden - Published 15 October 2026 Five people have been killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace. The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said they struck "the Saudi enemy's military operations headquarters in Aden".
news.full_article_text: Verified video footage showed smoke above the presidential palace in Aden - Published 15 October 2026 Five people have been killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace. The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said they struck "the Saudi enemy's military operations headquarters in Aden". A coalition led by Saudi Arabia backs the government and is providing air support for an offensive by pro-government forces against the Iran-backed Houthis. Yemeni health minister Qasim Buhaibeh said the casualties included "those working to guard the site and civilian employees". The country's Prime Minister Shaya Zindani condemned the Houthis' attack on Aden, calling it "cowardly" and a "continuation of their criminal behaviour". He said the government continued to carry out its duties and vowed that it would not weaken the resolve of its forces to continue operations against the Houthis on Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and other front lines. Earlier, the Houthis denied that they had attacked Saudi Arabia on Thursday, after the coalition said its forces had intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest shrines. The Houthis have been launching missiles and drones at airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the strikes on the territory that they control in western Yemen, including the capital Sanaa. On Saturday, a Houthi missile strike killed 13 people at Riyadh's international airport, which was the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia's deputy foreign minister accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis to escalate their conflict with the kingdom. "Iran continues to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN Security Council resolutions," Rayed Krimly told reporters, according to AFP news agency. "We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," he added. There was no immediate response from Iran's government. However, it has previously denied supplying weapons to the Houthis and said it only supports them politically. Iran's foreign minister has also said it is ready to provide "any assistance necessary to facilitate the start of talks" between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran. Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes. At least 1,282 people have been killed and 5,890 injured in the fighting in Yemen since 6 August, according to the government's health ministry. The UN says another 201,000 people have been displaced and that there has been an alarming surge in suspected cholera cases. hindi_translation.story_lead: सऊदी अरब के नेतृत्व वाले सैन्य गठबंधन ने रियाध की ओर दागे गए कई ड्रोन और मिसाइलों को सफलतापूर्वक नष्ट कर दिया। इस रक्षात्मक कार्रवाई ने सऊदी राजधानी पर संभावित हमलों को विफल कर दिया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### रियाध पर रक्षात्मक कार्रवाई
16 अक्टूबर 2026 को सऊदी नीत सैन्य गठबंधन की वायु रक्षा इकाइयों ने सऊदी अरब की राजधानी रियाध को निशाना बनाकर दागे गए सशस्त्र ड्रोन और मिसाइलों को सफलतापूर्वक निष्प्रभावी कर दिया।

### सुरक्षा अभियान
गठबंधन के सुरक्षा बलों ने हवाई खतरों का समय रहते पता लगाकर उन्हें शहरी क्षेत्र में स्थित लक्ष्यों तक पहुँचने से पहले ही नष्ट कर दिया। क्षेत्रीय हवाई क्षेत्र में निगरानी अभियान जारी है।
bullet_points: सऊदी नीत गठबंधन ने हवाई सुरक्षा प्रणालियों के जरिए ड्रोन और मिसाइलों को नष्ट किया।
हवाई हमलों का लक्ष्य सऊदी अरब की राजधानी रियाध थी।
वायु रक्षा बलों ने सभी खतरों को हवा में ही बेअसर किया।
यह घटना 16 अक्टूबर 2026 की है।

news.exam_corner_topic: Appointment of Governor of Sikkim
static_gk: Article 153 of the Constitution of India mandates that there shall be a Governor for each State.
Article 155 stipulates that the Governor of a State is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
Article 156 lays down that the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
news.headline: Sikkim Congress Protests Appointment of Dushyant Gautam as Governor
news.story_lead: The Sikkim Pradesh Congress Committee has staged protests opposing the central government's decision to appoint Dushyant Gautam as the Governor of Sikkim. The opposition party raised concerns over the political background of the appointee to the constitutional post.
news.full_article_text:
### Protests Over Gubernatorial Appointment

The Sikkim Congress unit organized demonstrations to voice opposition against the appointment of Dushyant Gautam as the Governor of Sikkim. The political unit expressed dissatisfaction with the selection made by the Union government.

### Constitutional Framework Governing State Governors

According to Article 155 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor of a State is appointed directly by the President of India. The controversy highlights recurring debates regarding political appointments to state gubernatorial offices and the necessity of maintaining constitutional neutrality.
bullet_points: Sikkim Pradesh Congress Committee initiated protests against Dushyant Gautam's appointment as Governor of Sikkim.
The appointment was officially highlighted on October 16, 2026.
The opposition party raised objections regarding political appointments to constitutional posts.
Under Article 155 of the Indian Constitution, State Governors are appointed by the President.
The development underscores constitutional discussions surrounding the role and neutrality of State Governors.
key_facts: Dushyant Gautam appointed as Governor of Sikkim.
Protests staged by the Sikkim Pradesh Congress Committee against the appointment.
important_dates: October 16, 2026: Protests reported in Sikkim against the appointment of Dushyant Gautam as Governor.
exam_relevance: Polity (GS Paper II): Constitutional provisions regarding the appointment, powers, and role of State Governors (Articles 153 to 161).
news.upsc_analysis: The appointment of Governors often becomes a subject of political debate when active political figures are appointed to constitutional posts. The Sarkaria Commission (1983) and the Punchhi Commission (2007) both recommended that Governors should be eminent individuals detached from local party politics to ensure administrative neutrality and seamless centre-state relations.
causes: Appointment of Dushyant Gautam as the Governor of Sikkim by the Union government.
impacts: Political demonstrations and objections raised by the local opposition Congress unit in Sikkim.
challenges: Maintaining institutional neutrality and political consensus in constitutional appointments.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Article 153: Executive head of the State.
Article 155: Appointment of the Governor by the President of India.
Article 156: Term of office of Governor.
way_forward: Adhering to recommendations of constitutional commissions such as the Sarkaria and Punchhi Commissions regarding the selection criteria for Governors.
news.mains_notes: The office of the Governor is crucial to Indian federalism as a constitutional link between the Union and States. Key recommendations include appointing detached, eminent personalities outside active politics to uphold non-partisan governance in state administration.
mains_questions: Discuss the constitutional role of the Governor under Article 155. What key reforms were suggested by the Sarkaria Commission to preserve the impartiality of this post?
Examine the friction points between state executives and gubernatorial appointments in federal setups.
news.takeaway: Sikkim Congress demonstrated against the appointment of Dushyant Gautam as the new Governor of Sikkim.
prelims_facts: State Governors are appointed by the President under Article 155 of the Indian Constitution.
Dushyant Gautam named Governor of Sikkim in October 2026.

hindi_translation.headline: दुष्यंत गौतम को राज्यपाल नियुक्त किए जाने के विरोध में सिक्किम कांग्रेस का प्रदर्शन
hindi_translation.story_lead: सिक्किम प्रदेश कांग्रेस कमेटी ने दुष्यंत गौतम को सिक्किम का राज्यपाल नियुक्त किए जाने के केंद्र सरकार के फैसले का विरोध किया है। विपक्षी पार्टी ने संवैधानिक पद पर की गई इस नियुक्ति पर आपत्ति जताई है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति पर विरोध

सिक्किम प्रदेश कांग्रेस कमेटी ने दुष्यंत गौतम को सिक्किम का राज्यपाल नियुक्त करने के फैसले के विरोध में प्रदर्शन किया। स्थानीय राजनीतिक दल ने केंद्र सरकार के इस चयन पर असंतोष व्यक्त किया।

### राज्यपाल नियुक्ति का संवैधानिक ढांचा

भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 155 के अनुसार, राज्य के राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है। यह विवाद संवैधानिक पदों पर नियुक्तियों और उनकी निष्पक्षता से जुड़ी चर्चाओं को पुनः उजागर करता है।
bullet_points: सिक्किम कांग्रेस ने दुष्यंत गौतम की सिक्किम के राज्यपाल के रूप में नियुक्ति का विरोध किया।
यह विरोध प्रदर्शन 16 अक्टूबर 2026 को सामने आया।
विपक्ष ने राजनीतिक पृष्ठभूमि वाले व्यक्तियों की संवैधानिक पदों पर नियुक्ति पर सवाल उठाए।
अनुच्छेद 155 के तहत भारत के राष्ट्रपति राज्यों के राज्यपालों की नियुक्ति करते हैं।
key_facts: दुष्यंत गौतम को सिक्किम का नया राज्यपाल नियुक्त किया गया।
सिक्किम प्रदेश कांग्रेस ने इस नियुक्ति के खिलाफ विरोध प्रदर्शन किया।
important_dates: 16 अक्टूबर 2026: सिक्किम में राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति के खिलाफ कांग्रेस का प्रदर्शन।
